     Bulgaria
     Q013 (General Comment): The Prosecutor's Office prepares a consolidated budget for all units, namely district, regional,
     military-regional, appellate, military-appellate prosecutor's offices, the administration of the European delegated prosecutors,
     training and rest bases and submits it to the Supreme Judicial Council (SJC). Pursuant to Article 361 of the Judicial System
     Act, the budget of the PRB includes all revenues from the activity, maintenance costs, relations with the central budget and
     other budgets.
     The budget procedure is carried out in two stages. First stage - preparation of a medium-term forecast for a period of three
     years. Second stage - preparation of a draft budget for the relevant year and updated budget forecasts for the next two years.
     The Minister of Justice proposes a draft budget for the judiciary and submits it for discussion in the Plenum of the SJC. The
     draft budget of the judiciary is accompanied by estimates for the next two years. The Council of Ministers submits to the
     National Assembly the draft law on the state budget of the Republic of Bulgaria for the relevant year together with the draft
     annual budget of the judiciary, proposed by the plenary session of the SJC, with a detailed justification. When adopting the
     state budget, the National Assembly listens to a report of the plenary session of the SJC, presented by its representative.
     The National Assembly adopts the budget of the judicial power, allocated to the SJC, the Inspectorate of the SJC, the bodies
     of the judicial power, including PRB and the National Institute of Justice (NIJ).
     The Plenum of the SJC organizes the execution of the budget of the judiciary through the Inspectorate of the SJC, the
     Supreme Court of Cassation, the Supreme Administrative Court, the courts, the Prosecutor General and the National Institute
     of Justice. The PRB is a second-level budget manager and all units of the PRB system are third-level budget managers. For
     third-level managers, the budget manager is the relevant manager.
     1. Preparation and presentation of a draft budget for the current budget year. The Law on the State Budget of the Republic of
     Bulgaria adopts the budget of the judiciary, including the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Bulgaria. By decree of the
     Council of Ministers, the main parameters and Guidelines for the implementation of the budget are given.
     2. Budget adjustments. Currently, during the calendar year, the Prosecutor General submits proposals for updating to the
     Budget and Finance Committee of the SJC

     transition accounts for the observed increase in budgetary allocation for training in 2023.
     More over, the costs associated with organizing training events have risen, including venue rentals, materials, and other
     logistical expenses. These cost increases also contribute to the higher budgetary needs for 2023.


     Q013 (2021): National Audit Office of Lithuania carried out an audit on the investigation and prevention of cybercrime, which
     aims to contribute to the creation of a safe environment for society in cyberspace. The audit recommendations highlighted the
     need for the General Prosecutor's Office to pay more attention to the development of competences in the investigation of
     cybercrime, as the competences of specialised prosecutors are not sufficiently enhanced due to an insufficient and
     unsystematic education system and the lack of methodologies for the investigation of cybercrime. Due to the high cost of
     cybercrime training, an additional budget was requested and a small part of it was received.



     Q013 (2020): In 2020 the decrease in the state budget funds allocated to the training of prosecutors was influenced by
     objective reasons. It should be noted that the Prosecutor’s Office participates in a wide range of international projects, from
     which it receives funding for capacity building activities. Also, individual trainings, traineeships and exchanges are funded by
     the European Judicial Training Network. In this context, there was no increased need for funds from the state budget for the
     training of prosecutors in 2020. In addition, the decrease in the need for allocations in this area has also been influenced by
     the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

     Question 037. Is there a system of compensation in the following circumstances:




     Austria
     Q037 (General Comment): : The Public Authority’s Liability Act (Amtshaftungsgesetz) provides for liability of the state (and
     other legal entities) for misconduct of their employees in the exercise of public authority, including court proceedings and court
     decisions, causing damage to persons or property by excessive length of proceedings, wrongful arrest and/or wrongful
     condemnation. The liability presupposes both wrongfulness and fault. In the case of wrongful arrest or wrongful criminal
     condemnation, compensation can also be obtained according to the Penal Law’s Compensation Act (Strafrechtliches
     Entschädigungsgesetz) without proving fault of the Authorities. The compensation procedure is laid down in para. 8 ff.
     Amtshaftungsgesetz and para. 9 ff. Strafrechtliches Entschädigungsgesetz. The injured person may demand – free of costs -
     of the legal entity against which the claim for damages is to be raised to forward her/him within a three months’ term a written
     statement indicating as to whether it accepts or partially or totally rejects the claim for damages. If the claim is partially or
     totally rejected, the complaint can still be filed at court. The exclusive jurisidiction over the claim of the injured person against
     the legal entity rests in the first instance with the regional court (Landesgericht) in charge of civil matters in whose range of
     jurisdiction the infringement of law occurred. Compensation is funded by the Public Authority’s general budget. The liability is
     unlimited, indemnity is to be paid in terms of money only. To make sure that compensation is paid following the concrete
     circumstances of each individual case, there is no such thing as a daily tariff or a flat compensation sum. The amount of
     compensation depends solely on the magnitude of damage suffered by the victim and the degree of fault attributable to the
     Public Authority. According to sec 67 CCP victims have the right to claim reimbursement for the damage caused by the
     criminal act or compensation for the impairment of their legally protected interests. The extent of the damage or the impairment
     has to be established ex officio as far as this can be done on the basis of the results of the criminal proceeding or with the help
     of additional simple investigations. If for the assessment of a bodily injury or damage to the health of a person an expert is
     appointed, he/she also has to be requested to establish the periods of pain.



     Q037 (2024): The payments according to the Public Authority’s Liability Act, European Convention on Human Rights and the
     Penal Law’s Compensation Act cannot be quantified regarding the different circumstances. Only the total amount
     of the payments can be provided. On this basis the payments according to the Public Authority’s Liability Act and the European
     Convention on Human Rights in the area of the courts were: € 524.788,14 and those according to the Penal Law’s
     Compensation Act were € 434.686,04 in 2024. The decrease of payments of more than 20% compared to the previous year is
     due to the fact that those payments are based on decisions by independent courts, which cannot be controlled by the judicial
     administration and are subject to strong fluctuations.

     Belgium
     Q037 (General Comment): In Belgian law, the term « inoperative pre-trial detention” is used instead of “wrongful arrest”.
     Compensation through the civil liability procedure:
     In Belgium, the State’s liability for damages resulting from faults committed by the public prosecutor’s office or judges falls
     under Article 1382 of the Civil Code according to which: “Any act whatsoever of a person which causes damage to another
     person obliges the person by whose fault it occurred to make reparation”. The fault may consist of negligence according to the
     terms of article 1383 which provides that “everyone is responsible for the damage he/she causes not only by his/her own act
     but also by his/her negligence or imprudence”. To obtain compensation, the plaintiff must prove the existence of a fault,
     damage and a causal link between the fault and the damage. According to the Constitutional Court (see Constitutional Court
     ruling of June 30th, 2014 (no. 99/2014)), a constitutionally correct interpretation of Article 1382 of the Civil Code implies that
     even if an erroneous decision is not repealed, modified, annulled, or revoked, the state can be held responsible for a serious
     mistake of a judge sitting at last instance. It is necessary that the mistake constitutes a sufficiently serious violation of the
     applicable rule of law and that, because of the limited appeal remedies available against the wrong decision, it is not possible
     to obtain the annulment of such decision. These claims are brought before civil courts.
     Exceeding the reasonable time of proceedings should also be considered as a fault. However, article 21ter of the Criminal
     Procedure Code provides for that in case the right to be judged within a reasonable time is violated, courts can either inflict
     lower sentence than the legal minimum sentence, or simply pronounce guilty verdict without imposing punishment. With regard
     to the State's liability for unlawful detention, Article 27 of the Act of March 13, 1973, on compensation for ineffective pre-trial
     detention provides for a right to compensation for any person who has been deprived of their liberty in conditions incompatible
     with the provisions of Article 5 of the ECHR.
     Reference should also be made to the Act of 13 March 1973 on compensation for inoperative pre-trial detention. Article 28 of
     this law provides for that "Any person who has been held in preventive detention for more than eight days without this
     detention or its continuation having been caused by his/her own conduct may claim compensation:
     a) if he or she has been directly or indirectly exempted from liability by a judicial decision that has become res judicata;
     b) if he/she has benefited from an order or a ruling of dismissal;
     c) if he/she has been arrested or kept in detention after the public action has been extinguished by prescription;
     The amount of such compensation shall be determined in equity, taking into account all the circumstances of public and
     private interest. If the person concerned is unable to bring an action for compensation before the ordinary courts, the
     compensation must be requested in writing to the Minister of Justice, who shall decide within six months. The compensation
     shall be granted by the Minister of Justice at the expense of the Treasury, if the conditions provided for in § 1 are met. If the
     compensation or the charge is refused, if the amount of the compensation or the number of days charged is deemed
     insufficient, or if the Minister of Justice has not taken a decision within six months of the request, the person concerned may
     apply to the Commission for Inoperative




     Pre-trial Detention.

     Bulgaria
     Q037 (General Comment): In the Republic of Bulgaria, there are two mechanisms for indemnification for damages. 1)The
     proceedings under the State and Municipalities Liability for Damages Act (SMLDA) aim to determine the procedure and
     grounds for holding the state and municipalities liable and for citizens and legal entities to receive compensation in cases of
     damage suffered as a result of unlawful acts, actions or omissions of state or municipal authorities and officials in the course of
     or in connection with the performance of administrative activities. Article 2 of SMLDA also regulates the liability of human rights
     bodies, including the prosecution service, whereby the state is liable for damage caused to citizens by the investigating
     authorities, the prosecution service or the court in the following cases: detention, including all cases of deprivation of liberty in
     violation of Article 5, § 1 of the ECHR; violation of rights protected by Article 5, § 2 – 4 of the Convention; charges for a crime if
     the person is found not guilty or if the criminal proceedings are dropped or the act has been amnestied; imposition of a penalty
     under the Criminal Code or an administrative penalty where the person is acquitted or the administrative penalty is annulled;
     application by the court of an administrative measure where its decision is annulled as unlawful; enforcement of a penalty
     imposed in excess of the specified term or amount; unlawful use of special intelligence means; an established violation
     committed by a pre-trial body through the disclosure of investigation materials in violation of the presumption of innocence or in
     a public statement in which the accused is presented as guilty; established violation of the rights of third parties under Section
     IX of Chapter Fourteen of the Criminal Procedure Code. Claims under Article 2, paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be examined by the
     courts in accordance with the procedure established in the Civil Procedure Code. Article 2b of SMLDA regulates the liability of
     the judicial authorities for violation of the right to have a case examined and decided within a reasonable time, in accordance
     with Article 6, §1 of the Convention. The courts shall determine the amount of compensation to be awarded on an equitable
     basis.
     2)The second legal indemnification mechanism is based on Chapter 3 “a” of the Judicial System Act that provides for the
     examination of applications by citizens and legal entities against acts, actions or omissions of the judicial authorities that
     violate their right to have their case examined and decided within a reasonable time.
     Applications may be submitted by citizens and legal entities who are: parties to concluded civil, administrative and criminal
     proceedings; defendants, victims or aggrieved legal entities in terminated pre-trial proceedings. Compensation for concluded
     or terminated proceedings shall be determined and paid in accordance with the practice of the ECrHR in an amount not
     exceeding BGN 10,000.
     Applications under paragraph 1 shall be submitted within six months of the conclusion of the relevant proceedings with a final
     act through the Inspectorate to the Supreme Judicial Council to the Minister of Justice. The Minister of Justice or a person
     authorised by him shall determine the amount of compensation (provided from the state budget ) in accordance with the
     practice of the ECHR and shall propose the conclusion of an agreement with the applicant. The circumstances shall be verified
     and a decision on the application shall be taken within six months of its receipt. Compensation shall be paid on the ba




     sis of the agreement concluded. Persons who have received compensation under this chapter may not seek compensation on
     the same grounds through the courts.
     A separate register shall be created for applications, which shall be published on the website of the Inspectorate to the
     Supreme Judicial Council. The Prosecutor's Office shall not keep statistics on compensation awarded under this procedure in
     connection with the activities of the Prosecutor's Office.
     No fee shall be payable for the examination of applications under this chapter.

     Q037 (2023): Prosecutor's Office of RB: In the Republic of Bulgaria, there are two mechanisms for indemnification for
     damages, in relation to the criminal proceedings.
     The first mechanism is regulated in the Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages Act. The state and the
     municipalities are liable for the damages caused to citizens and legal entities by unlawful deeds, acts or omissions of their
     authorities and officials in relation or with respect to the performance of an administrative activity, as well as for damages
     caused by the effect of secondary legislation revoked as being unlawful or declared null and void. Pursuant to Article 2 of this
     Act, the state is liable for damages caused to citizens by the investigation authorities, the prosecutor's office or the court in
     hypotheses determined in this text of the Act.
     Statistics is not maintained in the Prosecutor's Office, in the form of the indicators in the table in the present questionnaire. The
     data for year 2023 about the obtaining of a damage award against the Prosecutor's Office under the Liability of the State and
     Municipalities for Damages Act is, as follows:
     In 2023, the Prosecutor's Office lost suits filed by 292 persons under actions based on the legal grounds of Article 2 and Article
     2b of the Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages Act, as 281 court damage awards entered into force.
     Out of the legally effective 281 damage awards, 146 are based on granted actions based on the legal grounds of Article 2,
     Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 3, Option 1 of the Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages Act (legally effective
     acquittal), and 103 — based on the legal ground of Article 2, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 3, Option 2 of the Liability of the
     State and Municipalities for Damages Act (legally effective writ for the termination of the criminal proceeding).
     There are no legally effective court judgments based on the legal grounds of Article 2, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 2 of the
     Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages Act (violation of rights protected by Article 5, § 2-4 of the European
     Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms.)
     On the grounds of Article 2, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 1, Option 1 of the Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages
     Act, 7 damage awards were issued (unlawful detention in custody), which are legally effective.
     As regards actions based on the legal grounds of Article 2b of the Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages Act
     (violation of the right to hearing of the case within a reasonable time, in accordance with Article 6, § 1 of the European

     The second legal indemnification mechanism is provided for in the Judicial System Act (Chapter Three "a" of the Judicial
     System Act — consideration of applications against a violation of the right to hearing and resolution of the case within a

     This chapter governs the hearing of applications of citizens and legal entities against deeds, acts or omissions of the bodies of

     Q037 (2022): Prosecutor's Office of RB: In the Republic of Bulgaria, there are two mechanisms for compensation for damages
     in connection with criminal proceedings.
     The first mechanism is regulated in the Law on the Liability of the State and Municipalities for Damages (LLSMD). The state
     and municipalities are responsible for the damages caused to citizens and legal entities by illegal acts, actions or inactions of
     their bodies and officials during or on the occasion of the performance of administrative activities, as well as for the damages
     caused by the action of canceled as illegal or declared as null and void by-laws. According to Art. 2 of this law, the state is
     responsible for the damages caused to citizens by the investigative bodies, the prosecutor's office or the court in the
     hypotheses specified in this text of the law.
     The Prosecutor's Office does not keep statistics in the form of the indicators in the table in this questionnaire. The data for
     2022 regarding the conviction of the Prosecutor's Office under LLSMD are as follows:
     In 2022, the Prosecutor's Office was convicted by 255 persons on claims with a legal basis, Art. 2 and Art. 2b LLSMD, with 248
     convictions entering into force.

     Q037 (2024): The numbers in table 37 are based on data from Platina, which is a case management system used by The
     Danish Prosecution System. Data in table 37 has been created outside the standard data model. Specifically developed data
     models are tested, but still associated with a higher risk of unidentified errors compared to the standard model. Thus, the data
     in table 37 is associated with considerable uncertainty. The number of cases with a request for compensation corresponds to
     the number of distinct case reference numbers of relevant cases within the Regional State Prosecutors or the State Prosecutor
     for Special Crimes. The number of cases where a compensation has been granted, corresponds to the number of distinct case
     reference numbers of relevant cases within the Regional State Prosecutors, the State Prosecutor for Special Crimes or the
     Director of Public Prosecutions.
     The total sum of compensations is calculated as the sum of compensations in cases where the request for compensation has
     been either fully or partially granted by the Regional State Prosecutors, the State Prosecutor for Special Crimes or the Director
     of Public Prosecutions. It should be noted that cases in which a court has ordered The Danish Prosecution System to grant
     compensation are not included in table 37. This is because such cases are not registered in our case handling system
     (Platina). It should be noted that in Platina the amount of compensation granted is registered in a text-field where it is possible
     for the user to write characters other than numbers. Thus, there is a risk of some amounts not being included in the total if
     these are written in a way that means they cannot be converted in to a numerical value. In Platina, it is possible for a user to
     assign a case certain keywords. These keywords can later aid the identification of cases regarding a request for compensation
     that involve specific interventions, such as “arrests”, “pre-trial detentions” or “preliminary charges”. Since a single case may
     contain multiple keywords, but only one compensation amount, it is not possible to determine which specific interventions the
     compensation covers, or how the compensation is distributed if compensation was granted due to several different
     interventions. For this reason, a keyword-based classification is associated with such significant uncertainty that it is assessed
     that such a classification of numbers will provide an un-accurate representation of how request for compensation and
     compensations amounts are distributed across the categories ’Wrongful arrest/detention’ and ’Wrongful conviction’. We are
     aware that we, in previous contributions to CEPEJ’s evaluation, have provided data on request for compensation and
     compensations amounts divided into the categories ’Wrongful arrest/detention’ and ’Wrongful conviction’. However, we have
     subsequently become aware that previously used data models were subject to a significant uncertainty for the reason
     described above.

     Q037 (General Comment): The Legal Affairs Sub-Directorate of the Ministry of Justice, in conjunction with the State Judicial
     Officer, monitors liability actions relating to the malfunctioning of the public justice service (mainly based on Article L. 141-1 of
     the Code of Judicial Organisation, with regard to users of this service).
     The State Judicial Officer directly monitors actions for compensation for pre-trial detention in criminal proceedings that have
     ended in a decision to dismiss the case, acquittal, or discharge (Articles 149 et seq. of the Code of Criminal Procedure).
     1. With regard to liability actions relating to the malfunctioning of the public justice service:
     the vast majority of these are based on Article L. 141-1 of the Code of Judicial Organisation.
     Under this article, the State is required to compensate for damage caused by the malfunctioning of the justice service. Unless
     otherwise specified, this liability is only incurred in the event of gross negligence or denial of justice. This liability regime
     applies only to users of the public justice service, as third parties to legal proceedings can only invoke the State's strict liability
     for breach of equality before public burdens.
     With regard to actions brought on the basis of Article 149 et seq. of the Code of Criminal Procedure: article 149 of the CPC
     grants the right, under certain conditions, to full compensation for damage suffered as a result of detention in proceedings that
     have been dismissed, discharged, or acquitted.
     Any person who has been held in pre-trial detention during proceedings that have been terminated by a final decision to
     dismiss the case, acquit or discharge them is entitled, except in cases specifically defined in Article 149 of the CPC, to full
     compensation for the moral and material damage caused by such detention, upon request. The compensation awarded shall
     be paid by the State.
     The first president of the court of appeal in whose jurisdiction the decision to dismiss the case, acquit or discharge the
     detainee, thereby establishing their innocence, was handed down, shall rule, following a public and adversarial procedure, by
     means of a reasoned decision that may be appealed before the National Commission for the Compensation of Detentions
     attached to the Court of Cassation (CNRD).



     Q037 (2024): The figures provided with regard to the category “excessive length of proceedings” correspond to liability actions
     relating to the malfunctioning of the public justice service (Article L. 141-1 of the Code of Judicial Organization); the figures
     provided for the category “Unjustified arrest/detention” correspond to legal actions initiated on the basis of Article 149 et seq. of
     the Code of Criminal Procedure; the figures indicated for the category ‘Other’ correspond to disputes concerning “seals,”
     "police material damage” (broken doors) and “malfunctions of the public justice service due to gross negligence.”
     With regard to the compensation procedure (IDP) and the method of calculating the amount of compensation (e.g., the daily
     rate for an unjustified arrest or conviction):
     -there is no official scale for IDPs. They are assessed on a case-by-case basis, with reference to the case law of the CNRD,
     which applies relatively consistent amounts but without an official scale.
     The case law of the National Commission for the Compensation of Detentions (CNRD) and the Court of Cassation provides
     some numerical trends:
     • Moral damages: between €50 and €100 per day of detention on average (often around €1,500 to €3,000 per month)
     • Material damages: compensated on the basis of supporting documents (pay slips, employer certificates, economic losses).
     •In certain serious cases (very long detention, major psychological impact), the compensation may be much higher.
     In practice, unjustified detention can result in total compensation (moral + material) averaging around €25,000 to €26,000.
     Recent decisions illustrate a range from €10,000 for five months to €73,500 (moral + material damages + costs) for 20 months.

CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems

     Q037 (General Comment): According to the Act on Legal Redress for Excessive Length of Court Proceedings and of Criminal
     Investigation Proceedings (Gesetz über den Rechtsschutz bei überlangen Gerichtsverfahren und strafrechtlichen
     Ermittlungsverfahren) a person affected may file a complaint about undue delay (censure of delay) to the court seized of the
     case if proceedings seem unreasonably long. Subsequently, the person affected may bring a court action claiming
     compensation. The claim may be brought even before completion of the main proceedings. Adequate compensation is granted
     for pecuniary and nonpecuniary disadvantages. In criminal proceedings, the passage of time between the offence and the
     conviction, as well as the length of the proceedings, must also be taken into account and compensated ex officio by the court
     and the public prosecutor’s office in favour of the accused. Depending on the extent of the delay and the disadvantages
     suffered by the accused as a result, compensation may be provided by a ruling that a quantified part of the sentence imposed
     is already deemed to have been enforced (this will be stated in the operative part of the judgment). In individual cases, it may
     suffice – even at the investigation stage by the public prosecutor’s office – to discontinue proceedings (e.g. pursuant to
     Sections 153, 153a or 154 of the German Code of Criminal Procedure [Strafprozessordnung – StPO]), to dispense with
     imposing a penalty (Section 60 of the German Criminal Code [Strafgesetzbuch – StGB]) or, in the event of minor delays, to
     establish in the grounds of the judgment that the proceedings have been delayed in breach of the rule of law. In extreme
     cases, undue delay may constitute a procedural impediment that requires the court to terminate proceedings. If compensation
     has been provided in the criminal proceeding, except for compensation for material damage, the accused has received
     sufficient redress and is not further entitled to compensation in accordance with the Act on Legal Redress for Excessive Length
     of Court Proceedings and of Criminal Investigation Proceedings. If parties to a legal dispute suffer damage due to the
     excessive length of court proceedings, a compensation claim may also ensue under Section 839 of the German Civil Code
     (Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch – BGB) in conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz – GG). A claim under
     these provisions requires that an official intentionally or negligently breaches the official duty incumbent upon him in relation to
     a third party. If the official breaches his duties in a judicial decision in a legal matter, then the state is only liable if the breach of
     duty consists in a criminal offence. This limitation does not apply if the official refuses or delays the exercise of his duty.
     However, the manner in which a judge conducts the legal proceedings may only be examined for its justifiability due to the
     constitutional principle of judicial independence. If the official responsible for the execution of the court decision has delayed
     compulsory enforcement intentionally or negligently and in breach of his official duty, a compensation claim may ensue under
     Section 839 of the German Civil Code in conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law. A claim may also exist under
     Section 839 of the German Civil Code in conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law in cases of wrongful arrest if the
     official responsible intentionally or negligently breaches the official duty. Decisions by the judge responsible for matters of
     custody, as well as discretionary decisions by the pub




     lic prosecution office in criminal investigation proceedings, may, however, only be examined for their justifiability. In the case of
     a wrongful conviction a state liability claim requires that the judge responsible intentionally or negligently breaches the official
     duty in such a way that the breach of duty consists in a criminal offence.
     Anyone who has suffered damage from a criminal conviction is compensated by the Treasury if the conviction is quashed or
     reduced in reopened proceedings or otherwise in criminal proceedings after having become final and binding (Section 1(1) of
     the Act on Compensation for Criminal Prosecution Measures [Gesetz über die Entschädigung für Strafverfolgungsmaßnahmen
     – StrEG]). The same applies if a measure of correction and prevention or an ancillary measure has been ordered without a
     conviction (Section 1(2) StrEG). In cases of acquittal, discontinuation of the proceedings or refusal to initiate the main
     proceedings, Section 2(1) StrEG provides for compensation for the damage suffered inter alia due to the execution of remand
     detention or temporary arrest. Where the proceedings are discontinued in accordance with a discretional provision,
     compensation may be granted ex bono (Section 3 StrEG). The subject of the compensation is the property damage caused by
     the criminal prosecution measure. In cases of deprivation of liberty on the basis of a court ruling, this can also be immaterial
     damage (Section 7(1) StrEG). The current immaterial compensation is €75 for each day of deprivation of liberty commenced.

     Q037 (2020): According to the Act on Legal Redress for Excessive Length of Court Proceedings and of Criminal Investigation
     Proceedings (Gesetz über den Rechtsschutz bei überlangen Gerichtsverfahren und strafrechtlichen Ermittlungsverfahren) a
     person affected may file a complaint about undue delay (censure of delay) to the court seized of the case if proceedings seem
     unreasonably long. Subsequently, the person affected may bring a court action claiming compensation. The claim may be
     brought even before completion of the main proceedings. Adequate compensation is granted for pecuniary and non-pecuniary
     disadvantages.
     In criminal proceedings, the passage of time between the offence and the conviction, as well as the length of the proceedings,
     must also be taken into account and compensated ex officio by the court and the public prosecutor’s office in favour of the
     accused. Depending on the extent of the delay and the disadvantages suffered by the accused as a result, compensation may
     be provided by a ruling that a quantified part of the sentence imposed is already deemed to have been enforced (this will be
     stated in the operative part of the judgment). In individual cases, it may suffice – even at the investigation stage by the public
     prosecutor’s office – to discontinue proceedings (e.g. pursuant to Sections 153, 153a or 154 of the German Code of Criminal
     Procedure [Strafprozessordnung – StPO]), to dispense with imposing a penalty (Section 60 of the German Criminal Code
     [Strafgesetzbuch – StGB]) or, in the event of minor delays, to establish in the grounds of the judgment that the proceedings
     have been delayed in breach of the rule of law. In extreme cases, undue delay may constitute a procedural impediment that
     requires the court to terminate proceedings. If compensation has been provided in the criminal proceeding, except for
     compensation for material damage, the accused has received sufficient redress and is not further entitled to compensation in
     accordance with the Act on Legal Redress for Excessive Length of Court Proceedings and of Criminal Investigation
     Proceedings.
     If parties to a legal dispute suffer damage due to the excessive length of court proceedings, a compensation claim may also
     ensue under Section 839 of the German Civil Code (Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch – BGB) in conjunction with Article 34 of the
     German Basic Law (Grundgesetz – GG). A claim under these provisions requires that an official intentionally or negligently
     breaches the official duty incumbent upon him in relation to a third party. If the official breaches his duties in a judicial decision
     in a legal matter, then the state is only liable if the breach of duty consists in a criminal offence. This limitation does not apply if
     the official refuses or delays the exercise of his duty. However, the manner in which a judge conducts the legal proceedings
     may only be examined for its justifiability due to the constitutional principle of judicial independence.
     If the official responsible for the execution of the court decision has delayed compulsory enforcement intentionally or
     negligently and in breach of his official duty, a compensation claim may ensue under Section 839 of the German Civil Code in
     conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law.

     Q037 (General Comment): Excessive length: If the court is not able to finish the cases within reasonable time a compensation
     may be awarded to the parties. The court decides about the compensation in a fast tarck procedure. Non-execution of court
     decisions: Usually the court orders a 15 day deadline for fulfilling its final decision. If the party that is obliged to do so does not
     fulfil this obligation he/she also has to pay an interest from that day. Wrongful arrest: The damages occured for wrongful arrest,
     house arrest or preliminary detention at a psychiatric institution shall be compensated. Wrongful condemnation: If the person
     was convicted, but later - as a result of an extraordinary review procedure - he/she was not found guilty or received a lenient
     punishment. Any pecuniary punishment or cost of the procedure that was paid by the accused person should be repaid with
     interest included. Other: the court awards a compenstaion if the circumstances of the imprisonment of a convicted or arrested
     person violate his/her fundamental rights.

     Q037 (2024): Civil Proceedings
     Excessive Length of Proceedings (Civil Proceedings)
     In 2022, Act XCIV of 2021 on the enforcement of financial compensation related to the delay of civil litigation entered into
     force.
     According to the Hungarian civil procedural law there is a compensation for breach of the reasonable time requirement and
     also for not paying the monetary compensation. The consequences of the breach of the reasonable time requirement are
     regulated in the Act XCIV of 2021 on the enforcement of pecuniary compensation in connection with the protracted civil
     proceedings.
     Financial compensation is only available to the party who participated in the proceedings complained of, regardless of whether
     he or she was the successful or unsuccessful party. It is granted if the reasonable period of time specified by law is exceeded
     during the proceedings or a specific stage of the proceedings (according to the Hungarian laws, such stages are the first
     instance, the second instance and the review proceedings), and no concrete disadvantage needs to be proven.
     To determine the amount of pecuniary compensation, the duration of the proceedings or stage of proceedings to be taken into
     account must first be determined. This can be calculated by deducting from the duration of the proceedings or stage of
     proceedings calculated in accordance with the law the periods of time that are to be disregarded in accordance with the law.
     The period calculated in this way is subject to the payment of financial compensation if it exceeds the reasonable period laid
     down by law. In general, the duration of the entire court proceedings is considered reasonable if it does not exceed sixty
     months. The duration of the procedural stages is deemed reasonable if the duration of the proceedings at first instance does
     not exceed thirty months (or thirty-six months if the proceedings are initiated by an order for payment procedure), the duration
     of the proceedings at second instance eighteen months, and the duration of the review proceedings twelve months.
     For some actions (personal status, maintenance of a minor child, press vindication and employment) shorter time limits apply.
     In these cases, the duration of the entire court proceedings is considered reasonable if it does not exceed thirty-six months.
     The amount of the pecuniary compensation is the multiplication of the duration of the procedure (procedural stage) to be taken
     into account by four hundred forints per day.
     As of August 19th of 2025 according to Section 147/A of the Act CXXX of 2016 on the Code of Civil Procedure in case the time
     limit is overrun, the parties are entitled ex officio to monetary compensations, starting from the day after the time limit is
     overrun. The daily amount of monetary compensation is the 1,5 percent of the minimum wage (valid on the day of delay) and
     the courts are obligated to pay the monetary compensation for the entire duration of the time limit overrun.
     Non-execution of Court Decisions (Civil Proceedings)
     First of all, it should be noted that the fulfilment of judgments in civil proceedings is essentially voluntary. Consequently, if the
     unsuccessful party fails to fulfil the judgment voluntarily within a prescribed period of time, the successful party has the
     possibility to initiate enforcement proceedings. The costs of the enforcement procedure is borne by the unsuccessful party.
     According to the Hungarian laws in the case of a payment delay, the debtor is liable to pay interest for late payment from the
     date of the delay. It is important to note that this is not compensation, i.e. it is


     not necessary that the successful party suffers damages as a result of late payment.
     Criminal Proceedings
     Act XC of 2017 on Criminal Procedure (hereinafter: Be.) arranges in Chapter CVIII of its own right compensation in the case of
     unjustly limited and abstract leave. Compensation shall be payable for unlawful arrest, prior forced medical treatment and
     criminal supervision in which the defendant was required not to leave an apartment, other premises, institution or enclosed
     place without authorisation, and for detention ordered prior to the order of the accused person. In addition, compensation shall
     be granted to the accused person for imprisonment, imprisonment, education at a juvenile institution or forced treatment
     carried out on the basis of a final judgment, if he was subsequently acquitted as a result of an extraordinary remedy, the
     proceedings were terminated or a lesser penalty was imposed on him.
     The length of the criminal proceedings does not in itself constitute a ground for compensation, but the court may consider it as
     an attenuating circumstance when imposing the penalty, and then the Be. In accordance with Paragraph 562(1), the grounds
     of the court’s decision must state this.

     Criminal Proceedings
     Act XC of 2017 on Criminal Proceedings (hereinafter: Be.) regulates the recompense in case of unjustly limited and deprived
     liberty in a separate Chapter (Chapter CVIII – Recompense for unfounded restriction of freedom). Recompense shall be
     provided for any pre-trial detention, preliminary compulsory psychiatric treatment, criminal supervision during which, as
     prescribed by the court, the defendant was not allowed to leave a home, other premises, an institute or a fenced area of it
     without permission, or custody ordered before ordering any of the above. Recompense shall also be provided for any
     imprisonment, confinement, special education in a juvenile correctional institution, or compulsory psychiatric treatment
     enforced on the basis of a final and b


     inding judgment, provided that a court, as a result of extraordinary legal remedy acquitted the defendant with final and binding
     effect; imposed a less detrimental penalty on the defendant; terminated the proceeding against the defendant with a final and
     binding conclusive order. Protraction of the criminal proceedings does not in itself constitute a ground for recompense, but the
     court may take it into account as a mitigating circumstance when imposing the sentence. In this case, pursuant to Section 562
     (1) of Be., a reference to this fact shall be included in the short statement of reasons for the decision.
     In 2022, Act XCIV of 2021 on the enforcement of financial compensation related to the delay of civil litigation entered into
     force. The above data shows the results of the proceedings initiated under the new legislation.

     Q037 (2022): As regards private law, we highlight the possibility to enforce claims based on Act XCIV of 2021 on the
     Enforcement of Property Compensation for Delay in Civil Proceedings.
     The act defines the timeframe which may be regarded as reasonable and which is absolutely sufficient for the court to carry
     out the procedural steps necessary for a well-founded decision in the case.
     As a general rule, the duration of court proceedings is considered reasonable if it does not exceed sixty months from the date
     of commencement of the proceedings at first instance to the date of notification of the final decision closing the proceedings. A
     claim may also be brought in the event of a delay in the procedure phase. The duration of the procedural phase is considered
     reasonable if, for example, the duration of procedural phase at first instance does not exceed thirty months, the duration of
     procedural phase at second instance does not exceed eighteen months, and the duration of the review proceedings does not
     exceed twelve months. A shorter objective timeframe is set for specific cases that need to be dealt with quickly such as cases
     related to personal status, child support and employment. However, depending on the circumstances of a given case, the court
     seised may, at its judicial discretion, set a shorter timeframe as reasonable. A claim for compensation may be brought in
     relation to both pending and concluded cases if either the duration of the entire proceedings or a procedural phase exceeds
     the reasonable timeframe defined by law.
     If the duration of the court proceedings or procedural phase exceeds the timeframe considered reasonable, the party may
     claim monetary compensation from the court conducting the delayed proceedings at the rate set by government decree (HUF
     400,- per day). The compensation awarded is in proportion to the duration of the court proceedings. [see also the Government
     Decree 372/2021 (VI. 30.) on the amount of property compensation for delay in civil proceedings and the rules for calculating
     the amount to be paid.]
     Concerning criminal law, we would add that in case of an unlawful arrest, imprisonment, confinement, placement in a juvenile
     correctional institution or compulsory psychiatric treatment, a recompensation procedure as included in the Criminal
     Procedural Act, may be initiated. The person entitled to compensation may choose to enter into an agreement with the Ministry
     of Justice in a simplified procedure, in the framework of which a settlement is reached on the amount of the compensation, or
     to file a lawsuit and the court will decide on the amount of the compensation.
     In case of an agreement in the simplified compensation procedure, the compensation is adjusted to the number of days of
     unlawful deprivation of liberty, the amount per day is seven thousand forints (in the case of criminal supervision, the amount
     per day of compensation is three thousand five hundred forints).

     Luxembourg
     Q037 (General Comment): The law of 1st September 1988 concerning the civil liability of the State and public authorities
     permits the State to be held civilly liable before ordinary courts when a litigant alleges harm resulting from the defective
     functioning of judicial bodies. Examples of such dysfunction include excessive length of proceedings or a conviction stemming
     from judicial malpractice, which could form the basis of a claim. These complaints are typically brought before courts of first
     instance.

     Additionally, complaints about the excessive length of proceedings may also be pursued before the European Court of Human
     Rights (for violations of Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights) or could result in procedural sanctions during
     ongoing proceedings. However, the latter do not appear within the scope of our national systems. The involvement of various
     actors complicates the identification and categorisation of claims and compensation decisions, making it challenging to provide
     data that accurately reflects the broader situation.

     Nevertheless, we have been able to compile data on compensation for wrongful arrest/detention as regulated by the law of 30
     December 1981 on compensation for inoperative pre-trial detention. Available figures pertain to requests for compensation and
     decisions granting such compensation in cases of inoperative preventive detention (IPD)(https://mj.gouvernement.lu/fr/service-
     citoyens/detention-preventive.html), as well as the total amounts disbursed. It should be noted that, under the provisions of the
     law of 30 December 1981, the decisions are of administrative nature, rather than convictions.

     Q037 (2021): The law of 1 September 1988 on the civil liability of the State and public authorities allows the State to be held
     civilly liable before the ordinary courts if a person considers that he or she has been victim of a defective functioning of the
     judicial bodies. Excessive length of proceedings or a conviction resulting from such malfunctioning could be grounds for such
     an action. These complaints are brought before first instance courts. However, complaints about excessive length of
     proceedings can also be brought before the European Court of Human Rights (violation of Article 6 of the European
     Convention on Human Rights) or result in a procedural sanction during the proceedings. However, these last procedural steps
     do not appear in our systems. Thus, the diversity of the actors involved makes it difficult to identify the claims and decisions on
     compensation for the different categories and does not allow us to provide figures that reflect reality. However, it was possible
     to complete the table concerning compensation for wrongful arrest, provided for by the law of 30 December 1981, concerning
     compensation for inoperative preventive detention. The figures available for compensation for wrongful arrest represent the
     requests and decisions granting compensation for inoperative preventive detention (IPD) (https://mj.gouvernement.lu/fr/service-
     citoyens/detentionpreventive.html) as well as the total amount paid. We would like to point out, however, that in the context of
     the aforementioned law of 30 December 1981, it is not appropriate to speak of convictions, but of administrative decisions that
     can be appealed before the administrative courts.

     Q037 (General Comment): There is no mechanism for calculating the compensation. The courts take into consideration the
     national case law and the jurisprudence of the European Court of Human Rights in similar cases.
     Even if the civil regulations of material and procedural law do not provide special mechanisms for the compensation of
     individuals in case of excessive duration of procedures and non-enforcement of judgments, there are norms guaranteeing the
     right to a fair trial and at case settlement within a reasonable time-limit. In such circumstances, there is a possibility to pay
     certain sums of money as fines or even as a compensation. In criminal matters, the only possibility to obtain damages in case
     of procedural delays is the civil claim for damages, based on the provisions of the Civil Code. The Civil Procedure Code (the
     Law 134/2010) provides for a much more efficient mechanism to this effect, respectively the contestation concerning the
     protraction of the case settlement. Thus, according to Article 522 para. (1) of the CPC, any party, as well as the prosecutor
     attending the trial may make contestation by which, invoking the infringement of the right to the settlement of the trial within an
     optimal and reasonable time-limit, he/she solicits the adoption of legal measures remedying to this situation. Please, refer to
     the regulations of the CPC as concerns the guarantee of the right to a fair trial and a case settlement within a reasonable time-
     limit.
     The non-observance of judgments is incriminated as offence by Art. 287 of the Criminal Code. Within the criminal trial there
     may be also formulated the civil claim for damages for the non-enforcement of the judgment. The civil action may be also
     introduced separately, at the civil court. Both actions shall be judged according to the provisions of the Civil Code, regulating
     the delictual civil responsibility.
     Illegal arrest and illegal conviction are situations circumscribed to judicial errors for which the Romanian state is responsible
     according to Art. 538-539 and the following of the Criminal Procedure Code (the Law 135/2010). For the appreciation in
     substance of the civil responsibility, common law rules laid down by the Civil Code apply. According to the provisions of the art.
     538 of the Criminal Procedure Code, any person who suffered a wrongful condemnation or was, during a criminal trial, illegally
     deprived of his/her liberty is entitled to receive a compensation. The compensation should cover both the material and moral
     prejudices caused to that person. The amount of the compensation is to be determined by the court (the tribunal) in whose
     district the entitled person has its domicile. The entitled person should introduce a civil action against the state (which is
     represented by the Ministry of Public Finances), action which is exempted of any judicial fees.
     Regarding the excessive duration of the criminal procedures, there is a remedy, but it is not compensatory - see art. 488
     (index1) and the following of the Criminal Procedure Code. Law no. 201/2023 introduced a new article in the Criminal
     Procedure Code (the Law 135/2010) art. 359/1, stating the right to compensation for damage in the case of technical
     surveillance measures or activities specific to the collection of information illegally arranged ( 1 ) The person against whom he
     was ordered, confirmed, extended or illegally enforced a technical surveillance measure is entitled to compensation for the
     damage caused by this measure.

     Slovenia
     Q037 (General Comment): The Protection of Right to Trial without Undue Delay Act gives a party to court proceedings the
     right to have his rights, duties and any charges brought against him in his case before the court to be decided upon by the
     court without undue delay, as well as a right to compensation, if the aforementioned right was infringed.
     The procedure for compensation in the case of wrongful arrest and wrongful condemnation is regulated by the Criminal
     Procedure Act.
     The compensation, offered by the State Attorney’s Office for wrongful arrest varies from case to case, since circumstances of
     the individual case (e.g. length of wrongful arrest, effect on the injured person's family life and his closest social circle, effects
     of media exposure, effect to injured person's health, etc.), as well as court decisions in similar cases, are taken into account.
     The State Attorney's Office has its own budget to pay compensation in preliminary procedures. If a case goes to court, it
     usually becomes a long and complex process. Once the case is in court, compensation based on judgments or settlements is
     paid by the Ministry of Finance. To reach a court settlement, the State Attorney's Office must first get the Ministry’s approval.

     Spain
     Q037 (General Comment): Spanish legislation recognizes the right to compensation from the State in two generic cases,
     judicial error and abnormal functioning of the Administration of Justice and in a specific case of judicial error relating to pre-trial
     detention followed by acquittal or dismissal for lack of evidence. Cases of intentional or negligent conduct by the injured party
     and cases of force majeure are exempted. The request for compensation shall be processed in accordance with the rules
     regulating state liability. In cases of dolo (wilful misconduct) or gross negligence by judges or magistrates, the injured party
     may not directly sue them but shall address their request to the Ministry of Justice. The right to claim compensation has one
     year limitation period (statutory time-limit). The General Administration of the State may demand reimbursement from the
     responsible party once the injured party has been compensated. This will require that the dolo (wilful misconduct) or gross
     negligence of the judge or magistrate has been expressly recognized by a judgment or resolution issued by the General
     Council of the Judiciary. Article 121 Spanish Constitution and articles 292 et seq, Organic Law of the Judiciary, of July 1, 1985.

     Austria
     Q037 (General Comment): : The Public Authority’s Liability Act (Amtshaftungsgesetz) provides for liability of the state (and
     other legal entities) for misconduct of their employees in the exercise of public authority, including court proceedings and court
     decisions, causing damage to persons or property by excessive length of proceedings, wrongful arrest and/or wrongful
     condemnation. The liability presupposes both wrongfulness and fault. In the case of wrongful arrest or wrongful criminal
     condemnation, compensation can also be obtained according to the Penal Law’s Compensation Act (Strafrechtliches
     Entschädigungsgesetz) without proving fault of the Authorities. The compensation procedure is laid down in para. 8 ff.
     Amtshaftungsgesetz and para. 9 ff. Strafrechtliches Entschädigungsgesetz. The injured person may demand – free of costs -
     of the legal entity against which the claim for damages is to be raised to forward her/him within a three months’ term a written
     statement indicating as to whether it accepts or partially or totally rejects the claim for damages. If the claim is partially or
     totally rejected, the complaint can still be filed at court. The exclusive jurisidiction over the claim of the injured person against
     the legal entity rests in the first instance with the regional court (Landesgericht) in charge of civil matters in whose range of
     jurisdiction the infringement of law occurred. Compensation is funded by the Public Authority’s general budget. The liability is
     unlimited, indemnity is to be paid in terms of money only. To make sure that compensation is paid following the concrete
     circumstances of each individual case, there is no such thing as a daily tariff or a flat compensation sum. The amount of
     compensation depends solely on the magnitude of damage suffered by the victim and the degree of fault attributable to the
     Public Authority. According to sec 67 CCP victims have the right to claim reimbursement for the damage caused by the
     criminal act or compensation for the impairment of their legally protected interests. The extent of the damage or the impairment
     has to be established ex officio as far as this can be done on the basis of the results of the criminal proceeding or with the help
     of additional simple investigations. If for the assessment of a bodily injury or damage to the health of a person an expert is
     appointed, he/she also has to be requested to establish the periods of pain.

     Q037 (General Comment): In Belgian law, the term « inoperative pre-trial detention” is used instead of “wrongful arrest”.
     Compensation through the civil liability procedure:
     In Belgium, the State’s liability for damages resulting from faults committed by the public prosecutor’s office or judges falls
     under Article 1382 of the Civil Code according to which: “Any act whatsoever of a person which causes damage to another
     person obliges the person by whose fault it occurred to make reparation”. The fault may consist of negligence according to the
     terms of article 1383 which provides that “everyone is responsible for the damage he/she causes not only by his/her own act
     but also by his/her negligence or imprudence”. To obtain compensation, the plaintiff must prove the existence of a fault,
     damage and a causal link between the fault and the damage. According to the Constitutional Court (see Constitutional Court
     ruling of June 30th, 2014 (no. 99/2014)), a constitutionally correct interpretation of Article 1382 of the Civil Code implies that
     even if an erroneous decision is not repealed, modified, annulled, or revoked, the state can be held responsible for a serious
     mistake of a judge sitting at last instance. It is necessary that the mistake constitutes a sufficiently serious violation of the
     applicable rule of law and that, because of the limited appeal remedies available against the wrong decision, it is not possible
     to obtain the annulment of such decision. These claims are brought before civil courts.
     Exceeding the reasonable time of proceedings should also be considered as a fault. However, article 21ter of the Criminal
     Procedure Code provides for that in case the right to be judged within a reasonable time is violated, courts can either inflict
     lower sentence than the legal minimum sentence, or simply pronounce guilty verdict without imposing punishment. With regard
     to the State's liability for unlawful detention, Article 27 of the Act of March 13, 1973, on compensation for ineffective pre-trial
     detention provides for a right to compensation for any person who has been deprived of their liberty in conditions incompatible
     with the provisions of Article 5 of the ECHR.
     Reference should also be made to the Act of 13 March 1973 on compensation for inoperative pre-trial detention. Article 28 of
     this law provides for that "Any person who has been held in preventive detention for more than eight days without this
     detention or its continuation having been caused by his/her own conduct may claim compensation:
     a) if he or she has been directly or indirectly exempted from liability by a judicial decision that has become res judicata;
     b) if he/she has benefited from an order or a ruling of dismissal;
     c) if he/she has been arrested or kept in detention after the public action has been extinguished by prescription;
     The amount of such compensation shall be determined in equity, taking into account all the circumstances of public and
     private interest. If the person concerned is unable to bring an action for compensation before the ordinary courts, the
     compensation must be requested in writing to the Minister of Justice, who shall decide within six months. The compensation
     shall be granted by the Minister of Justice at the expense of the Treasury, if the conditions provided for in § 1 are met. If the
     compensation or the charge is refused, if the amount of the compensation or the number of days charged is deemed
     insufficient, or if the Minister of Justice has not taken a decision within six months of the request, the person concerned may
     apply to the Commission for Inoperative




     Pre-trial Detention.

     proceedings under the State and Municipalities Liability for Damages Act (SMLDA) aim to determine the procedure and
     grounds for holding the state and municipalities liable and for citizens and legal entities to receive compensation in cases of
     damage suffered as a result of unlawful acts, actions or omissions of state or municipal authorities and officials in the course of
     or in connection with the performance of administrative activities. Article 2 of SMLDA also regulates the liability of human rights
     bodies, including the prosecution service, whereby the state is liable for damage caused to citizens by the investigating
     authorities, the prosecution service or the court in the following cases: detention, including all cases of deprivation of liberty in
     violation of Article 5, § 1 of the ECHR; violation of rights protected by Article 5, § 2 – 4 of the Convention; charges for a crime if
     the person is found not guilty or if the criminal proceedings are dropped or the act has been amnestied; imposition of a penalty
     under the Criminal Code or an administrative penalty where the person is acquitted or the administrative penalty is annulled;
     application by the court of an administrative measure where its decision is annulled as unlawful; enforcement of a penalty
     imposed in excess of the specified term or amount; unlawful use of special intelligence means; an established violation
     committed by a pre-trial body through the disclosure of investigation materials in violation of the presumption of innocence or in
     a public statement in which the accused is presented as guilty; established violation of the rights of third parties under Section
     IX of Chapter Fourteen of the Criminal Procedure Code. Claims under Article 2, paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be examined by the
     courts in accordance with the procedure established in the Civil Procedure Code. Article 2b of SMLDA regulates the liability of
     the judicial authorities for violation of the right to have a case examined and decided within a reasonable time, in accordance
     with Article 6, §1 of the Convention. The courts shall determine the amount of compensation to be awarded on an equitable
     basis.
     2)The second legal indemnification mechanism is based on Chapter 3 “a” of the Judicial System Act that provides for the
     examination of applications by citizens and legal entities against acts, actions or omissions of the judicial authorities that
     violate their right to have their case examined and decided within a reasonable time.
     Applications may be submitted by citizens and legal entities who are: parties to concluded civil, administrative and criminal
     proceedings; defendants, victims or aggrieved legal entities in terminated pre-trial proceedings. Compensation for concluded
     or terminated proceedings shall be determined and paid in accordance with the practice of the ECrHR in an amount not
     exceeding BGN 10,000.
     Applications under paragraph 1 shall be submitted within six months of the conclusion of the relevant proceedings with a final
     act through the Inspectorate to the Supreme Judicial Council to the Minister of Justice. The Minister of Justice or a person
     authorised by him shall determine the amount of compensation (provided from the state budget ) in accordance with the
     practice of the ECHR and shall propose the conclusion of an agreement with the applicant. The circumstances shall be verified
     and a decision on the application shall be taken within six months of its receipt. Compensation shall be paid on the ba




     sis of the agreement concluded. Persons who have received compensation under this chapter may not seek compensation on
     the same grounds through the courts.
     A separate register shall be created for applications, which shall be published on the website of the Inspectorate to the
     Supreme Judicial Council. The Prosecutor's Office shall not keep statistics on compensation awarded under this procedure in
     connection with the activities of the Prosecutor's Office.
     No fee shall be payable for the examination of applications under this chapter.

CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems
in the EU Member States                                                                                                           1032 / 1444
     Q037 (2024): The numbers in table 37 are based on data from Platina, which is a case management system used by The
     Danish Prosecution System. Data in table 37 has been created outside the standard data model. Specifically developed data
     models are tested, but still associated with a higher risk of unidentified errors compared to the standard model. Thus, the data
     in table 37 is associated with considerable uncertainty. The number of cases with a request for compensation corresponds to
     the number of distinct case reference numbers of relevant cases within the Regional State Prosecutors or the State Prosecutor
     for Special Crimes. The number of cases where a compensation has been granted, corresponds to the number of distinct case
     reference numbers of relevant cases within the Regional State Prosecutors, the State Prosecutor for Special Crimes or the
     Director of Public Prosecutions.
     The total sum of compensations is calculated as the sum of compensations in cases where the request for compensation has
     been either fully or partially granted by the Regional State Prosecutors, the State Prosecutor for Special Crimes or the Director
     of Public Prosecutions. It should be noted that cases in which a court has ordered The Danish Prosecution System to grant
     compensation are not included in table 37. This is because such cases are not registered in our case handling system
     (Platina). It should be noted that in Platina the amount of compensation granted is registered in a text-field where it is possible
     for the user to write characters other than numbers. Thus, there is a risk of some amounts not being included in the total if
     these are written in a way that means they cannot be converted in to a numerical value. In Platina, it is possible for a user to
     assign a case certain keywords. These keywords can later aid the identification of cases regarding a request for compensation
     that involve specific interventions, such as “arrests”, “pre-trial detentions” or “preliminary charges”. Since a single case may
     contain multiple keywords, but only one compensation amount, it is not possible to determine which specific interventions the
     compensation covers, or how the compensation is distributed if compensation was granted due to several different
     interventions. For this reason, a keyword-based classification is associated with such significant uncertainty that it is assessed
     that such a classification of numbers will provide an un-accurate representation of how request for compensation and
     compensations amounts are distributed across the categories ’Wrongful arrest/detention’ and ’Wrongful conviction’. We are
     aware that we, in previous contributions to CEPEJ’s evaluation, have provided data on request for compensation and
     compensations amounts divided into the categories ’Wrongful arrest/detention’ and ’Wrongful conviction’. However, we have
     subsequently become aware that previously used data models were subject to a significant uncertainty for the reason
     described above.

     Q037 (General Comment): The Legal Affairs Sub-Directorate of the Ministry of Justice, in conjunction with the State Judicial
     Officer, monitors liability actions relating to the malfunctioning of the public justice service (mainly based on Article L. 141-1 of
     the Code of Judicial Organisation, with regard to users of this service).
     The State Judicial Officer directly monitors actions for compensation for pre-trial detention in criminal proceedings that have
     ended in a decision to dismiss the case, acquittal, or discharge (Articles 149 et seq. of the Code of Criminal Procedure).
     1. With regard to liability actions relating to the malfunctioning of the public justice service:
     the vast majority of these are based on Article L. 141-1 of the Code of Judicial Organisation.
     Under this article, the State is required to compensate for damage caused by the malfunctioning of the justice service. Unless
     otherwise specified, this liability is only incurred in the event of gross negligence or denial of justice. This liability regime
     applies only to users of the public justice service, as third parties to legal proceedings can only invoke the State's strict liability
     for breach of equality before public burdens.
     With regard to actions brought on the basis of Article 149 et seq. of the Code of Criminal Procedure: article 149 of the CPC
     grants the right, under certain conditions, to full compensation for damage suffered as a result of detention in proceedings that
     have been dismissed, discharged, or acquitted.
     Any person who has been held in pre-trial detention during proceedings that have been terminated by a final decision to
     dismiss the case, acquit or discharge them is entitled, except in cases specifically defined in Article 149 of the CPC, to full
     compensation for the moral and material damage caused by such detention, upon request. The compensation awarded shall
     be paid by the State.
     The first president of the court of appeal in whose jurisdiction the decision to dismiss the case, acquit or discharge the
     detainee, thereby establishing their innocence, was handed down, shall rule, following a public and adversarial procedure, by
     means of a reasoned decision that may be appealed before the National Commission for the Compensation of Detentions
     attached to the Court of Cassation (CNRD).




     Q037 (2024): The figures provided with regard to the category “excessive length of proceedings” correspond to liability actions
     relating to the malfunctioning of the public justice service (Article L. 141-1 of the Code of Judicial Organization); the figures
     provided for the category “Unjustified arrest/detention” correspond to legal actions initiated on the basis of Article 149 et seq. of
     the Code of Criminal Procedure; the figures indicated for the category ‘Other’ correspond to disputes concerning “seals,”
     "police material damage” (broken doors) and “malfunctions of the public justice service due to gross negligence.”
     With regard to the compensation procedure (IDP) and the method of calculating the amount of compensation (e.g., the daily
     rate for an unjustified arrest or conviction):
     -there is no official scale for IDPs. They are assessed on a case-by-case basis, with reference to the case law of the CNRD,
     which applies relatively consistent amounts but without an official scale.
     The case law of the National Commission for the Compensation of Detentions (CNRD) and the Court of Cassation provides
     some numerical trends:
     • Moral damages: between €50 and €100 per day of detention on average (often around €1,500 to €3,000 per month)
     • Material damages: compensated on the basis of supporting documents (pay slips, employer certificates, economic losses).
     •In certain serious cases (very long detention, major psychological impact), the compensation may be much higher.
     In practice, unjustified detention can result in total compensation (moral + material) averaging around €25,000 to €26,000.
     Recent decisions illustrate a range from €10,000 for five months to €73,500 (moral + material damages + costs) for 20 months.

     proceedings which have ended in a decision to dismiss, discharge or acquit that has become final, shall be entitled, subject to
     the exceptions precisely defined by Article 149 of the CCP, at his or her request, to full compensation for the moral and

     that can be appealed to the national commission for compensation for detention placed at the Court of Cassation (CNRD).
