     Q037 (General Comment): According to the Act on Legal Redress for Excessive Length of Court Proceedings and of Criminal
     Investigation Proceedings (Gesetz über den Rechtsschutz bei überlangen Gerichtsverfahren und strafrechtlichen
     Ermittlungsverfahren) a person affected may file a complaint about undue delay (censure of delay) to the court seized of the
     case if proceedings seem unreasonably long. Subsequently, the person affected may bring a court action claiming
     compensation. The claim may be brought even before completion of the main proceedings. Adequate compensation is granted
     for pecuniary and nonpecuniary disadvantages. In criminal proceedings, the passage of time between the offence and the
     conviction, as well as the length of the proceedings, must also be taken into account and compensated ex officio by the court
     and the public prosecutor’s office in favour of the accused. Depending on the extent of the delay and the disadvantages
     suffered by the accused as a result, compensation may be provided by a ruling that a quantified part of the sentence imposed
     is already deemed to have been enforced (this will be stated in the operative part of the judgment). In individual cases, it may
     suffice – even at the investigation stage by the public prosecutor’s office – to discontinue proceedings (e.g. pursuant to
     Sections 153, 153a or 154 of the German Code of Criminal Procedure [Strafprozessordnung – StPO]), to dispense with
     imposing a penalty (Section 60 of the German Criminal Code [Strafgesetzbuch – StGB]) or, in the event of minor delays, to
     establish in the grounds of the judgment that the proceedings have been delayed in breach of the rule of law. In extreme
     cases, undue delay may constitute a procedural impediment that requires the court to terminate proceedings. If compensation
     has been provided in the criminal proceeding, except for compensation for material damage, the accused has received
     sufficient redress and is not further entitled to compensation in accordance with the Act on Legal Redress for Excessive Length
     of Court Proceedings and of Criminal Investigation Proceedings. If parties to a legal dispute suffer damage due to the
     excessive length of court proceedings, a compensation claim may also ensue under Section 839 of the German Civil Code
     (Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch – BGB) in conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz – GG). A claim under
     these provisions requires that an official intentionally or negligently breaches the official duty incumbent upon him in relation to
     a third party. If the official breaches his duties in a judicial decision in a legal matter, then the state is only liable if the breach of
     duty consists in a criminal offence. This limitation does not apply if the official refuses or delays the exercise of his duty.
     However, the manner in which a judge conducts the legal proceedings may only be examined for its justifiability due to the
     constitutional principle of judicial independence. If the official responsible for the execution of the court decision has delayed
     compulsory enforcement intentionally or negligently and in breach of his official duty, a compensation claim may ensue under
     Section 839 of the German Civil Code in conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law. A claim may also exist under
     Section 839 of the German Civil Code in conjunction with Article 34 of the German Basic Law in cases of wrongful arrest if the
     official responsible intentionally or negligently breaches the official duty. Decisions by the judge responsible for matters of
     custody, as well as discretionary decisions by the pub




     lic prosecution office in criminal investigation proceedings, may, however, only be examined for their justifiability. In the case of
     a wrongful conviction a state liability claim requires that the judge responsible intentionally or negligently breaches the official
     duty in such a way that the breach of duty consists in a criminal offence.
     Anyone who has suffered damage from a criminal conviction is compensated by the Treasury if the conviction is quashed or
     reduced in reopened proceedings or otherwise in criminal proceedings after having become final and binding (Section 1(1) of
     the Act on Compensation for Criminal Prosecution Measures [Gesetz über die Entschädigung für Strafverfolgungsmaßnahmen
     – StrEG]). The same applies if a measure of correction and prevention or an ancillary measure has been ordered without a
     conviction (Section 1(2) StrEG). In cases of acquittal, discontinuation of the proceedings or refusal to initiate the main
     proceedings, Section 2(1) StrEG provides for compensation for the damage suffered inter alia due to the execution of remand
     detention or temporary arrest. Where the proceedings are discontinued in accordance with a discretional provision,
     compensation may be granted ex bono (Section 3 StrEG). The subject of the compensation is the property damage caused by
     the criminal prosecution measure. In cases of deprivation of liberty on the basis of a court ruling, this can also be immaterial
     damage (Section 7(1) StrEG). The current immaterial compensation is €75 for each day of deprivation of liberty commenced.

     Q037 (General Comment): Excessive length: If the court is not able to finish the cases within reasonable time a compensation
     may be awarded to the parties. The court decides about the compensation in a fast tarck procedure. Non-execution of court
     decisions: Usually the court orders a 15 day deadline for fulfilling its final decision. If the party that is obliged to do so does not
     fulfil this obligation he/she also has to pay an interest from that day. Wrongful arrest: The damages occured for wrongful arrest,
     house arrest or preliminary detention at a psychiatric institution shall be compensated. Wrongful condemnation: If the person
     was convicted, but later - as a result of an extraordinary review procedure - he/she was not found guilty or received a lenient
     punishment. Any pecuniary punishment or cost of the procedure that was paid by the accused person should be repaid with
     interest included. Other: the court awards a compenstaion if the circumstances of the imprisonment of a convicted or arrested
     person violate his/her fundamental rights.

     Q037 (2024): Civil Proceedings
     Excessive Length of Proceedings (Civil Proceedings)
     In 2022, Act XCIV of 2021 on the enforcement of financial compensation related to the delay of civil litigation entered into
     force.
     According to the Hungarian civil procedural law there is a compensation for breach of the reasonable time requirement and
     also for not paying the monetary compensation. The consequences of the breach of the reasonable time requirement are
     regulated in the Act XCIV of 2021 on the enforcement of pecuniary compensation in connection with the protracted civil
     proceedings.
     Financial compensation is only available to the party who participated in the proceedings complained of, regardless of whether
     he or she was the successful or unsuccessful party. It is granted if the reasonable period of time specified by law is exceeded
     during the proceedings or a specific stage of the proceedings (according to the Hungarian laws, such stages are the first
     instance, the second instance and the review proceedings), and no concrete disadvantage needs to be proven.
     To determine the amount of pecuniary compensation, the duration of the proceedings or stage of proceedings to be taken into
     account must first be determined. This can be calculated by deducting from the duration of the proceedings or stage of
     proceedings calculated in accordance with the law the periods of time that are to be disregarded in accordance with the law.
     The period calculated in this way is subject to the payment of financial compensation if it exceeds the reasonable period laid
     down by law. In general, the duration of the entire court proceedings is considered reasonable if it does not exceed sixty
     months. The duration of the procedural stages is deemed reasonable if the duration of the proceedings at first instance does
     not exceed thirty months (or thirty-six months if the proceedings are initiated by an order for payment procedure), the duration
     of the proceedings at second instance eighteen months, and the duration of the review proceedings twelve months.
     For some actions (personal status, maintenance of a minor child, press vindication and employment) shorter time limits apply.
     In these cases, the duration of the entire court proceedings is considered reasonable if it does not exceed thirty-six months.
     The amount of the pecuniary compensation is the multiplication of the duration of the procedure (procedural stage) to be taken
     into account by four hundred forints per day.
     As of August 19th of 2025 according to Section 147/A of the Act CXXX of 2016 on the Code of Civil Procedure in case the time
     limit is overrun, the parties are entitled ex officio to monetary compensations, starting from the day after the time limit is
     overrun. The daily amount of monetary compensation is the 1,5 percent of the minimum wage (valid on the day of delay) and
     the courts are obligated to pay the monetary compensation for the entire duration of the time limit overrun.
     Non-execution of Court Decisions (Civil Proceedings)
     First of all, it should be noted that the fulfilment of judgments in civil proceedings is essentially voluntary. Consequently, if the
     unsuccessful party fails to fulfil the judgment voluntarily within a prescribed period of time, the successful party has the
     possibility to initiate enforcement proceedings. The costs of the enforcement procedure is borne by the unsuccessful party.
     According to the Hungarian laws in the case of a payment delay, the debtor is liable to pay interest for late payment from the
     date of the delay. It is important to note that this is not compensation, i.e. it is


     not necessary that the successful party suffers damages as a result of late payment.
     Criminal Proceedings
     Act XC of 2017 on Criminal Procedure (hereinafter: Be.) arranges in Chapter CVIII of its own right compensation in the case of
     unjustly limited and abstract leave. Compensation shall be payable for unlawful arrest, prior forced medical treatment and
     criminal supervision in which the defendant was required not to leave an apartment, other premises, institution or enclosed
     place without authorisation, and for detention ordered prior to the order of the accused person. In addition, compensation shall
     be granted to the accused person for imprisonment, imprisonment, education at a juvenile institution or forced treatment
     carried out on the basis of a final judgment, if he was subsequently acquitted as a result of an extraordinary remedy, the
     proceedings were terminated or a lesser penalty was imposed on him.
     The length of the criminal proceedings does not in itself constitute a ground for compensation, but the court may consider it as
     an attenuating circumstance when imposing the penalty, and then the Be. In accordance with Paragraph 562(1), the grounds
     of the court’s decision must state this.

     Excessive Length of Proceedings (Civil Proceedings)

     Criminal Proceedings
     Act XC of 2017 on Criminal Proceedings (hereinafter: Be.) regulates the recompense in case of unjustly limited and deprived
     liberty in a separate Chapter (Chapter CVIII – Recompense for unfounded restriction of freedom). Recompense shall be
     provided for any pre-trial detention, preliminary compulsory psychiatric treatment, criminal supervision during which, as
     prescribed by the court, the defendant was not allowed to leave a home, other premises, an institute or a fenced area of it
     without permission, or custody ordered before ordering any of the above. Recompense shall also be provided for any
     imprisonment, confinement, special education in a juvenile correctional institution, or compulsory psychiatric treatment
     enforced on the basis of a final and b


     inding judgment, provided that a court, as a result of extraordinary legal remedy acquitted the defendant with final and binding
     effect; imposed a less detrimental penalty on the defendant; terminated the proceeding against the defendant with a final and
     binding conclusive order. Protraction of the criminal proceedings does not in itself constitute a ground for recompense, but the
     court may take it into account as a mitigating circumstance when imposing the sentence. In this case, pursuant to Section 562
     (1) of Be., a reference to this fact shall be included in the short statement of reasons for the decision.
     In 2022, Act XCIV of 2021 on the enforcement of financial compensation related to the delay of civil litigation entered into
     force. The above data shows the results of the proceedings initiated under the new legislation.

     Q037 (2022): As regards private law, we highlight the possibility to enforce claims based on Act XCIV of 2021 on the
     Enforcement of Property Compensation for Delay in Civil Proceedings.
     The act defines the timeframe which may be regarded as reasonable and which is absolutely sufficient for the court to carry
     out the procedural steps necessary for a well-founded decision in the case.
     As a general rule, the duration of court proceedings is considered reasonable if it does not exceed sixty months from the date
     of commencement of the proceedings at first instance to the date of notification of the final decision closing the proceedings. A
     claim may also be brought in the event of a delay in the procedure phase. The duration of the procedural phase is considered
     reasonable if, for example, the duration of procedural phase at first instance does not exceed thirty months, the duration of
     procedural phase at second instance does not exceed eighteen months, and the duration of the review proceedings does not
     exceed twelve months. A shorter objective timeframe is set for specific cases that need to be dealt with quickly such as cases
     related to personal status, child support and employment. However, depending on the circumstances of a given case, the court
     seised may, at its judicial discretion, set a shorter timeframe as reasonable. A claim for compensation may be brought in
     relation to both pending and concluded cases if either the duration of the entire proceedings or a procedural phase exceeds
     the reasonable timeframe defined by law.
     If the duration of the court proceedings or procedural phase exceeds the timeframe considered reasonable, the party may
     claim monetary compensation from the court conducting the delayed proceedings at the rate set by government decree (HUF
     400,- per day). The compensation awarded is in proportion to the duration of the court proceedings. [see also the Government
     Decree 372/2021 (VI. 30.) on the amount of property compensation for delay in civil proceedings and the rules for calculating
     the amount to be paid.]
     Concerning criminal law, we would add that in case of an unlawful arrest, imprisonment, confinement, placement in a juvenile
     correctional institution or compulsory psychiatric treatment, a recompensation procedure as included in the Criminal
     Procedural Act, may be initiated. The person entitled to compensation may choose to enter into an agreement with the Ministry
     of Justice in a simplified procedure, in the framework of which a settlement is reached on the amount of the compensation, or
     to file a lawsuit and the court will decide on the amount of the compensation.
     In case of an agreement in the simplified compensation procedure, the compensation is adjusted to the number of days of
     unlawful deprivation of liberty, the amount per day is seven thousand forints (in the case of criminal supervision, the amount
     per day of compensation is three thousand five hundred forints).

     Q037 (2023): We cannot indicate any specific reasons why the number of requests for compensation for damage out of court
     has significantly decreased. We also observe a consistent decrease in the number of persons applying to court for
     compensation for damage caused by unlawful actions of the state. We can perhaps attribute such a general trend to the fact
     that state institutions and officials make fewer mistakes that cause harm to individuals.
     From 2022-06-30, the legal regulation was changed, the amounts of damage that we compensate outside the court procedure
     were increased (property - no more than 10 thousand, non-property - no more than 5 thousand). However, the predictions that
     the number of requests would increase did not come true. Since the number of cases in courts is not increasing, it can be
     concluded that the institutions adhere to the human rights standard and try not to perform such actions that would be
     considered unlawful and cause harm (particularly positive changes are seen in criminal proceedings and in the execution of
     sentences).

     Luxembourg
     Q037 (General Comment): The law of 1st September 1988 concerning the civil liability of the State and public authorities
     permits the State to be held civilly liable before ordinary courts when a litigant alleges harm resulting from the defective
     functioning of judicial bodies. Examples of such dysfunction include excessive length of proceedings or a conviction stemming
     from judicial malpractice, which could form the basis of a claim. These complaints are typically brought before courts of first
     instance.

     Additionally, complaints about the excessive length of proceedings may also be pursued before the European Court of Human
     Rights (for violations of Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights) or could result in procedural sanctions during
     ongoing proceedings. However, the latter do not appear within the scope of our national systems. The involvement of various
     actors complicates the identification and categorisation of claims and compensation decisions, making it challenging to provide
     data that accurately reflects the broader situation.

     Nevertheless, we have been able to compile data on compensation for wrongful arrest/detention as regulated by the law of 30
     December 1981 on compensation for inoperative pre-trial detention. Available figures pertain to requests for compensation and
     decisions granting such compensation in cases of inoperative preventive detention (IPD)(https://mj.gouvernement.lu/fr/service-
     citoyens/detention-preventive.html), as well as the total amounts disbursed. It should be noted that, under the provisions of the
     law of 30 December 1981, the decisions are of administrative nature, rather than convictions.

     Q037 (General Comment): The rules for granting a sum of money in case of finding excessive length of proceedings are
     specified in the Act of 17 June 2004 on complaints of violation of the right of a party to hear a case in preparatory proceedings
     conducted or supervised by a prosecutor and court proceedings without unreasonable delay. According to art. 12 para. 4 of
     this Act, having regard to the complaint on (excessive), the court adjudicates from the Treasury, and in the case of complaints
     about the length of the proceedings conducted by the bailiff - from the bailiff, a sum of PLN 2,000 to PLN 20,000. The amount
     of the monetary sum, within the limits specified in the first sentence, is not less than PLN 500 for each year of the current
     duration of the proceedings, regardless of the number of stages of proceedings related to the excessive length of proceedings.
     The court may award a sum of money higher than PLN 500 for each year of the current duration of the proceedings, if the case
     is of particular importance to the applicant, who by his attitude did not contribute in a manner to prolonging the proceedings.
     This sum includes the amounts already awarded 16 to the applicant as a sum of money in the same case. No monetary sum is
     granted in the event of a complaint filed by the State Treasury or public sector units of the public finance sector.
     The accused, who was acquitted or condemned to a more lenient punishment as a result of the resumption of the proceedings
     or cassation, serves the State Treasury for damages and compensation for the harm suffered resulting from the execution of
     all or part of the punishment he was not supposed to incur. This provision shall also apply if the proceedings were discontinued
     after the convicting decision was abrogated as a result of circumstances which were not taken into account in the earlier
     proceedings. The right to compensation and redress also arises in connection with the application of a safeguard measure
     under the conditions laid down in those circumstances. Compensation and redress also apply in the event of undoubtedly
     unjustified detention or detention (Article 552 of the Code of Criminal Procedure).

     independent courts deciding on the legitimacy of claims and the amount of awarded compensation. The course of
     implementation of the expenditure plan in chapter 75595 during the budget year is therefore independent of the actions of the
     financial services of individual courts, because the payment of funds by the financial branch of the court, occurs only on the
     basis of a final court decision to pay compensation to the entitled person.

     of non-contractual civil liability of the State and other Public Entities, specifically providing for an autonomous regime of State
     liability for damages arising from the exercise of the judicial function (chapter III, arts. 12 to 14).

     Code, which provide for the right to compensation for illegal or unjustified deprivation of liberty by establishing a special
     regime. These articles also give effect to Article 27(5) CRP, which states that "Deprivation of liberty contrary to the provisions
     of the Constitution and the law shall constitute the State's duty to compensate the injured party under the terms established by
     law".

     Romania




CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems
in the EU Member States                                                                                                         1049 / 1444
     Q037 (General Comment): There is no mechanism for calculating the compensation. The courts take into consideration the
     national case law and the jurisprudence of the European Court of Human Rights in similar cases.
     Even if the civil regulations of material and procedural law do not provide special mechanisms for the compensation of
     individuals in case of excessive duration of procedures and non-enforcement of judgments, there are norms guaranteeing the
     right to a fair trial and at case settlement within a reasonable time-limit. In such circumstances, there is a possibility to pay
     certain sums of money as fines or even as a compensation. In criminal matters, the only possibility to obtain damages in case
     of procedural delays is the civil claim for damages, based on the provisions of the Civil Code. The Civil Procedure Code (the
     Law 134/2010) provides for a much more efficient mechanism to this effect, respectively the contestation concerning the
     protraction of the case settlement. Thus, according to Article 522 para. (1) of the CPC, any party, as well as the prosecutor
     attending the trial may make contestation by which, invoking the infringement of the right to the settlement of the trial within an
     optimal and reasonable time-limit, he/she solicits the adoption of legal measures remedying to this situation. Please, refer to
     the regulations of the CPC as concerns the guarantee of the right to a fair trial and a case settlement within a reasonable time-
     limit.
     The non-observance of judgments is incriminated as offence by Art. 287 of the Criminal Code. Within the criminal trial there
     may be also formulated the civil claim for damages for the non-enforcement of the judgment. The civil action may be also
     introduced separately, at the civil court. Both actions shall be judged according to the provisions of the Civil Code, regulating
     the delictual civil responsibility.
     Illegal arrest and illegal conviction are situations circumscribed to judicial errors for which the Romanian state is responsible
     according to Art. 538-539 and the following of the Criminal Procedure Code (the Law 135/2010). For the appreciation in
     substance of the civil responsibility, common law rules laid down by the Civil Code apply. According to the provisions of the art.
     538 of the Criminal Procedure Code, any person who suffered a wrongful condemnation or was, during a criminal trial, illegally
     deprived of his/her liberty is entitled to receive a compensation. The compensation should cover both the material and moral
     prejudices caused to that person. The amount of the compensation is to be determined by the court (the tribunal) in whose
     district the entitled person has its domicile. The entitled person should introduce a civil action against the state (which is
     represented by the Ministry of Public Finances), action which is exempted of any judicial fees.
     Regarding the excessive duration of the criminal procedures, there is a remedy, but it is not compensatory - see art. 488
     (index1) and the following of the Criminal Procedure Code. Law no. 201/2023 introduced a new article in the Criminal
     Procedure Code (the Law 135/2010) art. 359/1, stating the right to compensation for damage in the case of technical
     surveillance measures or activities specific to the collection of information illegally arranged ( 1 ) The person against whom he
     was ordered, confirmed, extended or illegally enforced a technical surveillance measure is entitled to compensation for the
     damage caused by this measure.

     Slovenia
     Q037 (General Comment): The Protection of Right to Trial without Undue Delay Act gives a party to court proceedings the
     right to have his rights, duties and any charges brought against him in his case before the court to be decided upon by the
     court without undue delay, as well as a right to compensation, if the aforementioned right was infringed.
     The procedure for compensation in the case of wrongful arrest and wrongful condemnation is regulated by the Criminal
     Procedure Act.
     The compensation, offered by the State Attorney’s Office for wrongful arrest varies from case to case, since circumstances of
     the individual case (e.g. length of wrongful arrest, effect on the injured person's family life and his closest social circle, effects
     of media exposure, effect to injured person's health, etc.), as well as court decisions in similar cases, are taken into account.
     The State Attorney's Office has its own budget to pay compensation in preliminary procedures. If a case goes to court, it
     usually becomes a long and complex process. Once the case is in court, compensation based on judgments or settlements is
     paid by the Ministry of Finance. To reach a court settlement, the State Attorney's Office must first get the Ministry’s approval.

     Spain
     Q037 (General Comment): Spanish legislation recognizes the right to compensation from the State in two generic cases,
     judicial error and abnormal functioning of the Administration of Justice and in a specific case of judicial error relating to pre-trial
     detention followed by acquittal or dismissal for lack of evidence. Cases of intentional or negligent conduct by the injured party
     and cases of force majeure are exempted. The request for compensation shall be processed in accordance with the rules
     regulating state liability. In cases of dolo (wilful misconduct) or gross negligence by judges or magistrates, the injured party
     may not directly sue them but shall address their request to the Ministry of Justice. The right to claim compensation has one
     year limitation period (statutory time-limit). The General Administration of the State may demand reimbursement from the
     responsible party once the injured party has been compensated. This will require that the dolo (wilful misconduct) or gross
     negligence of the judge or magistrate has been expressly recognized by a judgment or resolution issued by the General
     Council of the Judiciary. Article 121 Spanish Constitution and articles 292 et seq, Organic Law of the Judiciary, of July 1, 1985.

     Austria
     Q062-23 (2024): Administrative: Numbers above are for the Federal Administrative Court
     Regional administrative courts: DR: 95-100 %, UR: 50-75 %
     Supreme administrative court: 25-50 % deployment and usage rate
     Q062-24 (General Comment): An electronic case file system is used for the administration of investigative and court
     proceedings at public prosecutor's offices and courts. The case file system enables users to store, organise and structure
     documents as well as to use templates to create and sign documents electronically. Files can also be uploaded to the
     electronic case file. These files may also be dictated using speech-to-text applications, such as Dragon.
     Templates for LibreOffice are made available to all users. In addition, users can also create their own templates, so-called
     "structured short orders" for registry instructions and other tasks, using text modules and custom text samples. Automatically
     generated text is generally created by workflow rules and not by LLM-based artificial intelligence. LLM-based artificial
     intelligence is used for the anonymisation of documents.

     Q062-24 (2024): Regarding the Administrative Courts, not all functions are available in all the courts.
     Q062-25 (General Comment): Administrative: Numbers are for the Federal Administrative Court only! The others do not have
     tools for recording hearings yet.
     Q062-26 (General Comment): In recent years, the rate at which recording solutions have been deployed has steadily
     increased, and these systems are now implemented throughout the entire judicial system. Consequently, there are very few
     areas remaining where such solutions are not utilised—provided their application is considered appropriate. Notably, in
     criminal cases, audiovisual recordings of hearings are primarily employed, whereas in civil and administrative proceedings,
     dictation devices are predominantly used. These devices enable decision-making bodies to summarise and record the session
     in a concise protocol.

     Description for the ordinary courts and the Federal Administrative Court:
     Each court is equipped with a video recording system; additionally, decision-making bodies and court clerks may use mobile
     audio recording devices to document court proceedings. Audio and video files may be electronically entered into the case file
     and transmitted electronically to the parties. The automatic transcription of audio tracks using AI (including time stamps,
     speaker identification, etc.) is currently under evaluation. The decision whether to produce a summary protocol or a verbatim
     transcript lies with the decision-making body.


     Belgium




CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems

     Q062-23 (General Comment): Administrative matters (Council of State): for each type of procedure, there are template
     judgments containing certain standardised paragraphs. This standardisation particularly concerns the part relating to the
     conduct of the proceedings. Some documents are now generated automatically on the basis of information contained in
     internal databases (setting orders and hearing tables, for example).
     Strictly speaking, however, there are no ‘”writing assistance tools » for judgments.
     However, since 2017 all Council of State judgments have been written in direct style. This generalisation has ensured greater
     uniformity in the presentation of judgments. Council of State judges also have a number of tools at their disposal:
     a. Legal databases are maintained internally and also made available to the public (Juridict www.juridict.be , refLex
     www.reflex.be , etc.);
     b. Access is provided to private, paying legal databases (StradaLex www.stradalex.be , Jurisquare www.jurisquare.be, etc.);
     c. an intranet managed by the Council of State also centralises all documents produced by the Council of State (judgments,
     orders, reports, etc.). It is called Documap.
     d. The Council of State's website also offers numerous search options: www.raadvst-consetat.be.



     Q062-24 (General Comment): In civil and criminal matters:
     - most templates are available for all courts, or all templates are available for most courts - local modification of templates is
     always possible;
     - the options are not all part of the same application (e.g. speech-to-text)
     For speech-to-text: this is possible in the WORD application.
     Limitation: text generated automatically according to the Case Management Systems (CMS).
     Concerning electronic signature: only possible for justices of the peace; these courts are currently working with eSign to
     digitally sign documents. From 2025, police courts and criminal courts should also be able to sign electronically, followed by
     other courts.
     It is worth mentioning the JustCourt project, officially launched in 2024. This is a new tool that will enable virtual or hybrid
     hearings to be held in courts. It is currently being rolled out to cover all courts (scheduled for 2025–2026). Like other
     applications, JustCourt is part of the overall digitisation process undertaken by the FPS Justice to modernise and improve the
     Belgian judicial system for all its users.
     Q062-25 (General Comment): In May 2024, a new JustCourt tool was launched, enabling virtual or hybrid hearings to be held
     in Belgian courts. This involves installing videoconferencing systems in the courtrooms. This new application is part of the FPS
     Justice's digitisation initiative, which aims to modernise and improve the judicial system for all litigants. The pilot phase is
     currently underway. In civil and criminal matters: prior to the deployment of JustCourt: - in criminal matters, use of
     videoconferencing for research and investigations.
     - videoconferencing equipment was not available everywhere and systematically. Where necessary or appropriate, equipment
     could (also) be rented. Thanks to the new projects in this area, the availability of this equipment for the judiciary will be
     increased. In administrative matters - Council of State: the possibility exists in exceptional circumstances to hold a hearing by
     videoconference, but it is not foreseen to record it. It should be recalled that during the coronavirus crisis, a Royal Decree of
     Special Powers No. 12 (http://www.raadvstconsetat.be/?page=news&lang=fr&newsitem=592) enabled the Council of State to
     rule in writing and without a hearing, with the agreement of all the parties. In the same context, the Council of State was able to
     organise a number of remote hearings, virtually (via Skype or Teams), as part of the extreme emergency suspension
     procedure. This is still used on an ad hoc basis today, but to a very limited extent.


     Q062-26 (2024): The possibility of audio or audiovisual recording is enshrined in Article 759/2 of the Judicial Code, which
     states that "The court before which the public hearing is taking place may decide, on an exceptional basis, to record that public
     hearing where such audio or audiovisual recording is of interest for the creation of historical archives of the justice system or
     for educational purposes with a view to imparting knowledge in the field of law or the functioning of the justice system, with the
     consent of the persons whose voices and images are recorded, each for their own part. This consent may be withdrawn at any
     time during the hearing. (...)" (provision introduced by a law of April 25, 2024).



     Bulgaria




CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems
in the EU Member States                                                                                                         1061 / 1444
     Q062-24 (General Comment): “Speech to text” – By Decision under Protocol No. 25/29.09.2023, the Plenum of the Supreme
     Judicial Council approved and implemented in all judicial bodies the software created under the project "Development and
     implementation in the judicial system of software for accelerated creation and reproduction of acts and other documents
     through dictation and automatic conversion of voice recording into text /voice-to-text/ and accompanying processing systems",
     according to which the SJC is a beneficiary in a contract financed under the Operational Program "Good Governance" 2014-
     2020. The "voice-to-text" (V2T) system is a tool for digitization and allows magistrates instead of manually type their acts, to
     dictate and receive automatically typed text, allowing for quick formatting, searching and bolding words, referencing,
     annotation and other options for additional text processing and references to all key segments of the acts. The software for
     accelerated creation and reproduction of acts and other documents through dictation and automatic conversion of voice
     recording into text /voice-to-text/ is of the "artificial intelligence" type. It was developed using the "deep neural networks"
     method and of key importance for its effectiveness was training through voice recordings of words, through audio recordings of
     judicial and prosecutorial acts, that correspond to maximum extent to the real use of terminology in judicial practice. The
     system supports the following file formats:
     WAV (Waveform audio), *.wav;
     AIFF (Audio Interchange File Format), *.aif;
     FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec), *.flac;
     MP3 (MPEG Audio-1 Layer 3), *.mp3;
     AAC (Advanced Audio Coding), *.m4a, *.m4b, *.m4p, *.m4v, *.m4r, *.3gp, *.mp4, *.aac;
     WMA (Windows Media Audio), *.wma;
     OGG (Vorbis), *.ogg.
     The supported text formats are:
     MS Word, *.doc, *.docx);
     Rich Text Format, *.rtf;
     Plain Text Format, *.txt;
     Portable Document Format, *.pdf.
     On 05.06.2024, the Operational Program "Good Governance" published information in the Information System for
     Management and Monitoring of EU Funds in Bulgaria (ISMM) about the successful fulfillment of all SJC obligations and,
     accordingly, about the project completion.
     “Templates” – The Unified Information System of Courts (UISC) contains templates for judicial acts, such as decisions, orders,
     rulings, etc. As an example of how it works, we provide the steps for the preparation of a decision. After the judge enters the
     specific hearing and selects the necessary act, a window is generated in the UISC, where only the motivation and dispositive
     parts of the act are entered. After filling in the necessary fields and sequentially selecting the buttons "record", "prepare an act"
     and "send for signature", the complete decision is generated. This also applies to other types of acts, i.e. the judge does not
     write the title part, but only the motivation and dispositive parts.

     Croatia
     Q062-26 (General Comment): The implementation of the Audio Recording and Transcription System for court hearings is
     currently underway. The contract with the Contractor was signed on March 28, 2025. The deadline for the completion of the
     procurement is 18 months from the date of contract signing.
     At the moment, work is being carried out on establishing a central software solution for the integration of all courts into a
     unified system for monitoring and managing a shared repository of all recordings, as well as a central software solution for the
     automated transcription of recordings stored in the central shared repository. After completion implementation will proceed in
     individual courtrooms (a total of 1,317 courtrooms).


     Czech Republic
     Q062-24 (General Comment): The use of writing assistance tools in courts depends on the type of agenda and the
     information system used. Some systems automatically generate documents based on templates, data, and selected
     procedural actions. Older systems use an external application called APSTR, which helps create documents but is only
     available for district courts.
     Document templates are developed either by the Ministry of Justice or at the national level in cooperation with experts and
     court staff. These templates can be modified locally by individual courts or even by users, allowing for adjustments to specific
     court agendas. However, not all types of cases are covered by these templates. Additionally, speech-to-text tools are available
     for all courts.
     Q062-25 (General Comment): Recording of court hearings has been compulsory in all matters in the form of audio or
     audiovisual recordings since 2009. While the implementation of recording systems progressed gradually in previous years due
     to hardware, software, and funding limitations, significant progress was made in 2023-2024. Several key digitalisation projects
     were completed, resulting in a substantial increase in coverage. Currently, approximately 95–100% of court hearings are
     recorded.

     Q062-26 (2024):
     Whether civil, criminal, economic, or administrative, court hearings can now be recorded or filmed for reasons of public
     interest, for educational, informational, cultural, or scientific purposes. Article 38 quater of the law of July 29, 1881, on the
     freedom of the press sets the legal framework for the recording and broadcasting of hearings and was supplemented by
     Decree No. 2022-462 of March 31, 2022. This legal framework only allows same-day broadcasting of hearings before the
     Council of State and the Court of Cassation. Within this framework, in 2024, the latter recorded and broadcast seven hearings
     of its solemn formations (Plenary Assembly and mixed chambers) on the same day, held in both civil and criminal matters.

     Hungary
     Q062-24 (General Comment): In 2022, writing assistance tools were made available to all employees working within the entire
     court system. These were licensed tools that staff members tried and tested. Based on user feedback, it was determined by
     2023 that, considering the specific characteristics of the Hungarian language and the legal terminology, these tools did not
     improve the efficiency of court work. Their language recognition functions were not easily scalable, and therefore, they were
     phased out. Simultaneously, we sought new solutions and acquired cloud-based tools that, although previously restricted by
     legal regulations, could now be developed and trained. These tools were fewer in number than in the past.

     Q062-26 (General Comment): A ViaVideo system has been implemented nationwide. Every police station has at least one
     room equipped with it, every penitentiary institution has several rooms, and every court in the country has at least one
     courtroom — in some cases more — equipped with the system. It transmits both audio and video simultaneously and is also
     capable of recording hearings. The recorded material is saved in a format suitable for use by the court. The system also allows
     other participants — for instance, the prosecutor, defence counsel, expert witness, or a party/defendant/witness— to join the
     hearing via a link sent by e-mail. If the judge uses this system to make a continuous audio and video recording of the hearing,
     the recording itself constitutes the official record (minutes). In such cases, a written summary must be prepared from the
     recording. This summary contains only technical information — such as who appears on the recording and during which time
     interval, and what procedural act took place — but not the substantive content of those acts.

     Q062-26 (General Comment): Court hearings are recorded by use of DAR (Digital Audio Recordings). Audio recordings are
     made for internal court purposes and are under the control of the court. They are not generally available to parties or to the
     public, unless ordered by the Court although applications can be made to the court for a transcript of the recording, or part
     thereof for a fee. For example, this might arise if court proceedings are subject to a Judicial Review in a higher court.

     Latvia
     Q062-24 (General Comment): In Latvian courts, writing and text processing support tools are used to ensure consistent
     document quality and to facilitate daily work. The central platform is the Court Information System, which serves as the main
     environment for preparing, storing, and managing judicial documents. It provides pre-defined templates, allows text formatting
     in line with regulatory requirements, and enables automated case registration, helping judges and staff maintain consistency in
     documentation.
     An important element is the integration with the e-Case platform, which allows procedural documents to be submitted and
     received electronically, as well as the use of digital signatures, thereby reducing the circulation of paper documents. Writing
     support is also ensured by language and terminology tools – text editors with Latvian spell-check functionality and access to
     legal databases that help secure the accuracy of judgments and other procedural documents.
     Since 2024, Latvian courts have been gradually testing speech recognition solutions that automatically convert hearing audio
     recordings into text. These tools are still in the testing phase, and human verification remains essential, but in the long run,
     they are expected to reduce manual transcription work and speed up the preparation of protocols. In addition, document
     generation tools are employed to quickly produce standard rulings, summons, or notifications, reducing repetitive drafting.
     Writing assistance also extends to secure electronic communication forms, ensuring that information provided to parties is
     clear, standardized, and in full compliance with procedural requirements. Together, these tools form a solid foundation for
     more efficient court operations and improved quality of judicial documentation.

     Q062-24 (General Comment): Writing assistance tools are available across civil, administrative and criminal courts, and they
     provide a set of functionalities designed to support and streamline the drafting of judicial and administrative acts.
     The main features include:
     •Pre-defined templates: Users have access to a wide library of standardized templates for different procedural acts. The
     system guides the user to select the appropriate template based on their profile and the type of action to be performed,
     ensuring consistency across courts. In many cases, the user does not need to add any text and only needs to sign the
     document; however, they may still edit or adjust the content if desired.
     •Automatically generated text: The courts’ system provides automatic texts that users can use. These indicate the process, the
     intended recipient, and the action to be performed, and users may also add observations.
     •Electronic signature: All documents drafted through these tools can be finalised and authenticated using a qualified electronic
     signature, ensuring legal validity.
     Additional contextual notes:
     •A language simplification initiative was implemented to make certain standard texts clearer and more accessible, particularly
     when addressing natural and legal persons.
     •The system also provides spelling and text correction, as well as automatic text suggestions for routine formulations. Users
     may add specific remarks or tailor content when necessary, even within automatically generated acts.
     Overall, these tools support efficiency, uniformity, and quality in the preparation of documents across all jurisdictions.

     Romania
     Q062-24 (2024): (See general comments)
     Q062-26 (General Comment): In Romania’s judicial system, the integrated solution OPTIMUS has been implemented.
     Developed in-house, it manages audio recordings and automatic voice-to-text transcription. It is “cloud ready” and uses
     machine learning algorithms to identify speakers. The solution underwent a successful technological pilot that evaluated its
     performance in challenging acoustic environments. The project is continuing with integration into the national case
     management system, ECRIS V, as part of the PNRR investment titled “Development of integrated audio recording systems in
     courtrooms and automatic transcription components.”
     1. Technical Clarifications Regarding Automatic Indexing
     Automatic indexing of recordings is achieved through speaker change detection and automatic segmentation of the audio
     stream (diarization). Machine learning algorithms identify transitions between speakers and automatically mark key moments
     in the recording, generating time markers used for both audio navigation and alignment of sound segments with the
     transcribed text.
     2. General Context Regarding Courtroom Session Recording
     Audio recording of courtroom sessions is a standard component of judicial activity. The OPTIMUS solution streamlines the
     transcription process and helps reduce drafting time. The implementation uses dedicated equipment for audio capture,
     separate from general sound systems. Nationally, the project aims to acquire the necessary IT infrastructure and equip over
     1,000 courtrooms with specific devices, with data processing and integration to be carried out through the centralized
     infrastructure of ECRIS V.

     Bulgaria
     Q062-24 (General Comment): “Speech to text” – By Decision under Protocol No. 25/29.09.2023, the Plenum of the Supreme
     Judicial Council approved and implemented in all judicial bodies the software created under the project "Development and
     implementation in the judicial system of software for accelerated creation and reproduction of acts and other documents
     through dictation and automatic conversion of voice recording into text /voice-to-text/ and accompanying processing systems",
     according to which the SJC is a beneficiary in a contract financed under the Operational Program "Good Governance" 2014-
     2020. The "voice-to-text" (V2T) system is a tool for digitization and allows magistrates instead of manually type their acts, to
     dictate and receive automatically typed text, allowing for quick formatting, searching and bolding words, referencing,
     annotation and other options for additional text processing and references to all key segments of the acts. The software for
     accelerated creation and reproduction of acts and other documents through dictation and automatic conversion of voice
     recording into text /voice-to-text/ is of the "artificial intelligence" type. It was developed using the "deep neural networks"
     method and of key importance for its effectiveness was training through voice recordings of words, through audio recordings of
     judicial and prosecutorial acts, that correspond to maximum extent to the real use of terminology in judicial practice. The
     system supports the following file formats:
     WAV (Waveform audio), *.wav;
     AIFF (Audio Interchange File Format), *.aif;
     FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec), *.flac;
     MP3 (MPEG Audio-1 Layer 3), *.mp3;
     AAC (Advanced Audio Coding), *.m4a, *.m4b, *.m4p, *.m4v, *.m4r, *.3gp, *.mp4, *.aac;
     WMA (Windows Media Audio), *.wma;
     OGG (Vorbis), *.ogg.
     The supported text formats are:
     MS Word, *.doc, *.docx);
     Rich Text Format, *.rtf;
     Plain Text Format, *.txt;
     Portable Document Format, *.pdf.
     On 05.06.2024, the Operational Program "Good Governance" published information in the Information System for
     Management and Monitoring of EU Funds in Bulgaria (ISMM) about the successful fulfillment of all SJC obligations and,
     accordingly, about the project completion.
     “Templates” – The Unified Information System of Courts (UISC) contains templates for judicial acts, such as decisions, orders,
     rulings, etc. As an example of how it works, we provide the steps for the preparation of a decision. After the judge enters the
     specific hearing and selects the necessary act, a window is generated in the UISC, where only the motivation and dispositive
     parts of the act are entered. After filling in the necessary fields and sequentially selecting the buttons "record", "prepare an act"
     and "send for signature", the complete decision is generated. This also applies to other types of acts, i.e. the judge does not
     write the title part, but only the motivation and dispositive parts.

     Portugal
     Q062-24 (General Comment): Writing assistance tools are available across civil, administrative and criminal courts, and they
     provide a set of functionalities designed to support and streamline the drafting of judicial and administrative acts.
     The main features include:
     •Pre-defined templates: Users have access to a wide library of standardized templates for different procedural acts. The
     system guides the user to select the appropriate template based on their profile and the type of action to be performed,
     ensuring consistency across courts. In many cases, the user does not need to add any text and only needs to sign the
     document; however, they may still edit or adjust the content if desired.
     •Automatically generated text: The courts’ system provides automatic texts that users can use. These indicate the process, the
     intended recipient, and the action to be performed, and users may also add observations.
     •Electronic signature: All documents drafted through these tools can be finalised and authenticated using a qualified electronic
     signature, ensuring legal validity.
     Additional contextual notes:
     •A language simplification initiative was implemented to make certain standard texts clearer and more accessible, particularly
     when addressing natural and legal persons.
     •The system also provides spelling and text correction, as well as automatic text suggestions for routine formulations. Users
     may add specific remarks or tailor content when necessary, even within automatically generated acts.
     Overall, these tools support efficiency, uniformity, and quality in the preparation of documents across all jurisdictions.

     Q062-26 (General Comment): In recent years, the rate at which recording solutions have been deployed has steadily
     increased, and these systems are now implemented throughout the entire judicial system. Consequently, there are very few
     areas remaining where such solutions are not utilised—provided their application is considered appropriate. Notably, in
     criminal cases, audiovisual recordings of hearings are primarily employed, whereas in civil and administrative proceedings,
     dictation devices are predominantly used. These devices enable decision-making bodies to summarise and record the session
     in a concise protocol.

     Description for the ordinary courts and the Federal Administrative Court:
     Each court is equipped with a video recording system; additionally, decision-making bodies and court clerks may use mobile
     audio recording devices to document court proceedings. Audio and video files may be electronically entered into the case file
     and transmitted electronically to the parties. The automatic transcription of audio tracks using AI (including time stamps,
     speaker identification, etc.) is currently under evaluation. The decision whether to produce a summary protocol or a verbatim
     transcript lies with the decision-making body.

     hearing where such audio or audiovisual recording is of interest for the creation of historical archives of the justice system or

     recording. This summary contains only technical information — such as who appears on the recording and during which time
     interval, and what procedural act took place — but not the substantive content of those acts.

CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems
in the EU Member States                                                                                                         1080 / 1444
     Q062-26 (General Comment): In Romania’s judicial system, the integrated solution OPTIMUS has been implemented.
     Developed in-house, it manages audio recordings and automatic voice-to-text transcription. It is “cloud ready” and uses
     machine learning algorithms to identify speakers. The solution underwent a successful technological pilot that evaluated its
     performance in challenging acoustic environments. The project is continuing with integration into the national case
     management system, ECRIS V, as part of the PNRR investment titled “Development of integrated audio recording systems in
     courtrooms and automatic transcription components.”
     1. Technical Clarifications Regarding Automatic Indexing
     Automatic indexing of recordings is achieved through speaker change detection and automatic segmentation of the audio
     stream (diarization). Machine learning algorithms identify transitions between speakers and automatically mark key moments
     in the recording, generating time markers used for both audio navigation and alignment of sound segments with the
     transcribed text.
     2. General Context Regarding Courtroom Session Recording
     Audio recording of courtroom sessions is a standard component of judicial activity. The OPTIMUS solution streamlines the
     transcription process and helps reduce drafting time. The implementation uses dedicated equipment for audio capture,
     separate from general sound systems. Nationally, the project aims to acquire the necessary IT infrastructure and equip over
     1,000 courtrooms with specific devices, with data processing and integration to be carried out through the centralized
     infrastructure of ECRIS V.

     Q132 (General Comment): Judges/prosecutors are first placed into a certain pay grade according to their position within the
     judiciary system (e.g. regional courts, supreme court, administrative courts, etc.), where they receive the according base salary
     (§ 66 RStDG / § 190 RStDG). Every four years the salary increases by a fixed amount up until a certain maximum. Judges and
     public prosecutors in certain senior positions, such as the head of a district court, the vice president or president of a court of
     first instance or the head of a senior public prosecutor's office/public prosecutor's office, are entitled to a service allowance
     (between EUR 201.40 and EUR 1560.60 as at 31 Dezember 2024). The service allowance is part of the monthly salary. The
     service allowance is part of the monthly payment together with the salary. In principle, it could be stated that the salary covers
     all additional work performed by judges and public prosecutors in terms of quantity and time. Administrative Courts: First
     instance professional judge at the beginning of his/her career: Gross annual salary: EUR 86440 Net annual salary: EUR 55850
     Judge of the Administrative Supreme Court: Gross annual salary: approx. EUR 150000

     Q132 (General Comment): The gross amount of 86,916 corresponds to the salary of a judge in a court of first instance at the
     start of their career (= between 3 and 6 years of seniority) and that of a deputy public prosecutor at the start of their career (=
     between 3 and 6 years of seniority).
     The amount of 158,926 corresponds to the salary of a counselor at the Court of Cassation with the maximum length of service
     (given that appointment to the Court of Cassation is the final stage of a judicial career for each of them, they all receive the
     maximum). The salaries of administrative judges are not included in the table. Counselors to the Council of State are not part
     of the judicial system. Their salaries are also set by law.
     Salary evolves according to financial seniority with an increase every three years. The calculation of net salary depends on
     individual parameters (based on the situation of the person concerned, married, number of dependent children etc.) and
     therefore cannot be described in general terms. The following are deducted from the gross salary: health insurance
     contributions, survivor's pension contributions, special social security contribution, withholding tax.

     Q132 (General Comment): The gross salary of a Supreme court judge is formed as the sum of the Basic Monthly Salary for
     the Position of "supreme judge or prosecutor" (BMSP) + Rank + Additional remuneration for time served. The Rank and BMSP
     are determined according to the Classifier of Positions in the Administration of Courts and Prosecutors' offices, which are
     approved by decisions of the Judges' and the Prosecutors' College of the Supreme Judicial Council, respectively. The
     additional remuneration for time served is determined as 2% of (BMSP+Rank) is added for each year of service in the judicial
     system.
     Q132 (2023): According to Art. 218, paragraph 3 of the Judiciary System Act (JSA), the remuneration of judges, prosecutors
     and investigators is determined by a decision of the General Assembly of the Supreme Judicial Council (SJC) and the
     Supreme Prosecutorial Council (SPC) that adopts "Table No. 1 - for determination of the maximum basic monthly salaries of
     judges, prosecutors and investigators", which is applicable for all magistrates equally. In this regard, data for judges and
     prosecutors match completely. The gross monthly remuneration of judges, prosecutors and investigators is formed by adding
     to the basic monthly remuneration the remuneration for rank (from Table No. 1) and time served (according to Article 219 of
     the JSA).

     Comment from the Supreme Court of Cassation: The amount of maximum basic monthly remuneration of judges shall be
     determined by the Plenum of the Supreme Judicial Council. Judges shall receive additional remuneration for long service and
     professional experience, determined in relation to the basic remuneration at the rate of up to 40% (2% – for 1 calendar year for
     acquired service and professional experience in a judicial authority; 1.5% – for 1 calendar year for acquired service and
     professional experience outside a judicial authority, but in the same time, similar or the same nature of work, position or
     profession; 1% – for 1 calendar year for acquired service and professional experience outside a judicial authority and in
     another specialty). The maximum amount of 40% is set by the Judicial System Act, in force since 11.08.2007. Judges who
     reached a higher percentage before the amendment of the law shall retain the percentage reached in accordance with the
     decision of the Supreme Judicial Council under Protocol No.29/21.09.2007. In the Supreme Court of Cassation, 14 judges
     receive additional remuneration in excess of 40%. Judges don't get a 13th salary or bonuses paid regularly to everyone,
     regardless of their personal circumstances. By a decision of the Plenum of the Supreme Judicial Council, an additional
     remuneration may be paid to judges, but its receipt is not mandatory and unconditional. The entitlement to receive an
     additional remuneration is defined in the Rules for Determination and Payment of Additional Remuneration (adopted by a
     decision of the Plenum of the Suprem


     e Judicial Council under Protocol No. 29/22.11.2018, amended and supplemented by a decision under Protocol No.
     13/13.06.2019, amended and supplemented by a decision under Protocol No. 28/21.11.2019, amended and supplemented by
     a decision under Protocol No. 18/12.05.2022 and the Rules for Determination and Payment of Additional Remuneration to
     Judges pursuant to Article 233, paragraph 6, the first sentence of the Judiciary System Act (adopted by the Judicial Collegium
     of the Supreme Judicial Council by Decision under Protocol No. 24/22.06.2021, amended by Decision under Protocol No.
     41/17.11.2021). In 2022 additional remuneration in the amount of 11,220 BGN or 5,736.69 EUR was paid to the judges of the

     of the Rules for Determination and Payment of Additional Remuneration. (Gross annual salary, in €= basic salary+ additional

     Q052 (General Comment): The category “other” encompasses judicial trainees or staff in charge of court documentation, as
     well as press center and telephone exchange staff.
     The judicial trainee is entitled to perform the acts of the court under the conditions and to the extent specified in factual and
     time plan of the preparatory service which is compiled by the chairman of the regional court after consultation with the advisory
     board for the education of trainees. The plan must be focused in such a way that the training for the performance of the
     function of a judge serves in particular to:
     a) deepening the trainee's professional knowledge of substantive and procedural law,
     b) developing the trainee's ability to apply legislation in a specific matter,
     c) gaining knowledge of individual agendas maintained by courts and their implementation,
     d) acquisition of procedural procedures and habits necessary for the performance of the function of a judge,
     e) acquaintance with ethical principles related to the performance of the function of a judge.
     In accordance with the preparatory service plan, the trainee performs preparatory service at a district or regional court. The
     trainee is usually assigned to one judge. Familiarization with individual court agendas is ensured by the fact that the president
     of the court where the judicial trainee is currently located gradually assigns the trainee to individual court departments.
     The preparatory service includes adaptation courses, seminars and lectures organized by the Judicial Academy and
     educational activities organized by court for at least 2 days per month.
     Starting from 2022 the title of “judicial trainee” has been replaced with “judicial candidate”.

     Q055 (General Comment): The National Prosecution Authority comprises the Office of the Prosecutor General that acts as
     the general administrative unit, and five prosecution districts: Southern Finland, Western Finland, Northern Finland, Eastern
     Finland and Åland. The National Prosecution Authority has 34 offices around Finland. The Prosecutor General is the supreme
     prosecutor and the head of the prosecution service. The Prosecutor General directs and develops prosecutorial activity by
     issuing general instructions and guidelines to the prosecutors. She/he also appoints district prosecutors. The Prosecutor
     General may take over a case from a prosecutor, but cannot order a prosecutor to decide the case in any given manner.
     She/he can also self-decide on the bringing of charges and designate a prosecutor to pursue the case in the courts. The
     Deputy Prosecutor General decides the matters in his/her competence on the same authority as the Prosecutor General.
     He/she also acts as a deputy for the Prosecutor General when necessary. For regular prosecutorial tasks, the Office of the
     Prosecutor General has state prosecutors whose jurisdiction covers the entire country. Most criminal matters (about 91 3000
     cases annually) are dealt with by the prosecution areas. The Office of the Prosecutor General deals mainly with criminal cases
     with wider significance to society as a whole, a few dozen every year. Prosecutors in Finland are not bound on Court
     instances, and every prosecutor is expected to, in a normal situation, to handle and prosecute the criminal case all the way to
     the Supreme Court, if needed.

     Q132 (2022): In Finland, there are several salary categories for judges. The salary depends also on the years of work
     experience. At the end of 2022 first instance judge is in a salary category T11 in which the gross salary is from 4944,63
     €/month to 6428,019€/month depending on his/her experience. A permanent first instance judge T13 has usually at least nine
     years of work experience which means the salary is 6036,7065 €/month. In Finland, the taxation is progressive so the
     information on net salary varies from person to person and is not available.
     Prosecutors salaries are based on three components: task-specific , personal component and component based on the years
     of employment. At the start of the career prosecutors usually start at the lower levels of task-specific paylevels, as well as the
     component based on years of employment is lower. By your own capability you can rise your own personal component.
     Experienced professionals usually have higher levels in all three components.



     Q132 (2020): Prosecutors in Finland are not bound on Court instances.
     Q132 (2016): In Finland there are several salary categories for judges. The slary depends also on the experience. A first
     instance judge has a category of T 11 for which the gross salary is from 4501,79 €/month to 5627,24 €/month depending on
     his/her experience. A permanent 1st instance judge has usually at least 9 years experience which means the salary is 5177,06
     €/month. In Finland we have progressive taxation so the information on net salary is not available.

     Q146 (General Comment): As of 2014, only attorneys-at-law, public legal aid lawyers and licenced legal counsels are allowed
     to represent a client in court. In addition, in-house lawyers can represent their company in court. Lawyers working for trade
     unions can represent a client in a district court and in the Labour Court in disputes regarding employment relationship.
     Lawyers working for public authorities can represent the public authority in court.
     In order to qualify as an attorney-at-law, a lawyer needs to have at least four years of work experience and must pass the
     demanding three-part professional qualification test known as the bar examination. The titles of attorney-at-law and attorney’s
     office are protected by law and can only be used by lawyers accepted into the Finnish Bar Association. Attorney's offices
     employ also associate lawyers, that is lawyers who are not yet members of the bar.

     Q057 (General Comment): In France there are other persons having similar duties to those of public prosecutors, namely the
     so called "délégués du procureur". The latter carry out certain tasks of the public prosecutor: implementing alternative
     measures to criminal prosecution, notifying measures proposed as part of a penal composition, notifying convicted offenders of
     penal orders, monitoring the implementation of probationary sentences, monitoring the enforcement of penalty sentences,
     receiving payment of fines imposed by penal order, representing the public prosecutor in territorial bodies.




CEPEJ study on the functioning of judicial systems
in the EU Member States                                                                                                        1163 / 1444
     Q057 (2023): The ”délégués du procureur” carry out functions comparable to those of public prosecutors. They intervene to
     implement alternative measures to prosecution decided by the public prosecutor for minor offences (reminder of obligations
     under the law, conditional discontinuation, penal composition). They may also be tasked with issuing summonses to appear in
     court or criminal orders. They carry out their duties within the premises of first instance courts, courts of appeal or any place of
     justice designated by the public prosecutor (points of justice, police stations, etc.). As key players in the local justice system,
     their duties have been extended and diversified as part of the reform to make criminal proceedings more efficient, as set out in
     decree no. 2020-1640 of 21 December 2020. They can now hold office hours, represent the public prosecutor at meetings of
     partnership bodies or receive payment of fines.

     Q057 (2022): In France there are other persons having similar duties to those of public prosecutors, namely the so called
     "délégués du procureur". The latter carry out certain tasks of the public prosecutor: implementing alternative measures to
     criminal prosecution, notifying measures proposed as part of a penal composition, notifying convicted offenders of penal
     orders, monitoring the implementation of probationary sentences, monitoring the enforcement of penalty sentences, receiving
     payment of fines imposed by penal order, representing the public prosecutor in territorial bodies.

     In 2022, there were 1 004 "délégués du procureur". The number in full time equivalent is 400 and it has been calculated
     approximately, as they work on a sessional basis.

     Q057 (2016): No other person has functions comparable to those of the public prosecutor, the latter being sole in charge of the
     public prosecution. On the other hand, certain powers may be delegated on an ad hoc basis within a specific framework. Thus,
     before the police court and the local court which are competent to try contraventions of the first four levels, the functions of the
     public prosecutor are carried out by an officer of the public prosecutor's office (OMP) in the person of the competent police
     commissioner in the jurisdiction of these courts.
     The prosecutor of the Republic may also designate a representative of the public prosecutor to intervene in the procedure of
     criminal composition or to remind the perpetrator of the obligations resulting from the law, to direct the perpetrator to a health,
     social or professional structure or to ask the perpetrator to regularise his/her situation or to compensate the damage resulting
     from the offence. The prosecutor's delegates may be natural persons or associations. They are empowered to do so by the
     public prosecutor, must take an oath before the court and are bound by professional secrecy. They submit an annual activity
     report to the prosecutor.
     The prosecutor's delegates are not members of the public prosecutor's office and are not in charge of initiating public
     prosecutions, unlike the officers of the public prosecutor's office mentioned above. Indeed, the prosecutor's delegates are only
     competent within the framework of the mission assigned to them for an alternative measure to prosecution in a specific case.

     Q132 (General Comment): Administrative courts:
     First-instance professional judge at the beginning of their career: the data mentioned in the first line corresponds to the
     average salary of a junior advisor at the first-grade level.
     Judge of the Supreme Court or final appellate court: this refers to the average salary of deputy presidents of the litigation
     section. The salary primarily consists of: base salary: this depends on the increased index held by the civil servant in their
     grade and step within the grade, and it progresses with seniority according to an index scale. This index is multiplied by the
     value of the public service point to calculate the base salary; additional remuneration components: paid based on personal
     circumstances (e.g., dependents, location of the administrative residence, allowances for assignments in certain overseas
     territories, etc.); allowances: either paid on a fixed basis depending on the various functions that may be held during the career
     or based on the significance and quality of the service rendered, and the achievement of quantitative objectives.

     Civil and criminal courts:
     The average salary of a first-instance professional judge at the beginning of their career corresponds to the entry-level salary
     upon starting their position after completing the National School for the Judiciary (ENM).
     The average salary of a first-instance prosecutor at the beginning of their career corresponds to the entry-level salary upon
     starting their position after completing the ENM.
     The average salary of judges at the Court of cassation (the methodology used in previous years is applied): it is more relevant
     to take the average cost of judges at the Court of Cassation, as it should reflect the highest salary of a judge/prosecutor in the
     highest judicial instance, rather than the salary of the president of the court or the Attorney General.
     Prosecutor at the Supreme Court or final appellate court: same as above.

     "Pact for the Rule of Law" (Pakt für den Rechtsstaat):
     The federal level and the Länder on 31 January 2019 agreed on a ‘Pact for the Rule of Law’. The pact foresees additional
     funding of EUR 220 million from the federal level for the Länder to create 2000 additional posts for judges and prosecutors,
     including the necessary administrative staff by 31 December 2021. In addition, the federal level is creating 24 additional posts
     at the Federal Court of Justice and 71 posts at the Prosecutor General of the Federal Court of Justice. New posts that were
     created after the beginning of 2017 are included into the count.
     A joint report by the Federal Government and the Länder on the state of implementation of the pact was presented on 10 June
     2021. The report concluded that the implementation has well progressed, noting in particular that over 2 700 post for judges
     and prosecutors have been created so far, with 2 500 being filled.
     These numbers will not be reflected directly in the data given above, because the figures represent the average value of the
     actual personnel deployed during the reference year (in full-time equivalents).
     It should also




      be noted that one of goals of the ‘Pact for the Rule of Law’ is to address the challenges related to the upcoming wave of
     retirements of judges and public prosecutors.
